title: Director of Government Affairs
description:
About Endurance

Endurance is building the world's first modular subsea geothermal power plants, converting vast thermal resources under the ocean into gigawatts of baseload power. Backed by Founders Fund, Felicis, First Round Capital, and Point72 Ventures, our founding team includes veterans from SpaceX, Helion, Blue Origin, and Apple. We have completed multiple deep-ocean deployments to subsea volcanoes and are launching a long-term demonstration project this fall. By leveraging modular design, manufacturing scale, efficient drilling, and latent cooling on the seafloor, we are pioneering a new category of energy that outperforms traditional sources on environmental impact, deployment speed, and cost.

What You’ll Be Doing

As the Director of Government Affairs, you will own relationships, partnerships, and policy engagement with defense programs. This person is our principal voice at the ONR, NAVSEA Warfare Centers, DARPA, other DoD S&T enterprise, and acquisition program offices, with the Military Departments, and on the Hill committees that shape defense energy and installation resilience.

This role will play an instrumental role shaping requirements, positions Endurance Energy for programs and funding, and gives leadership early, accurate read on the Department of Defense (DoD) acquisition and budget cycle. The Director works within the office of Policy and External Affairs; works closely with the commercial, engineering, and legal teams; and represents the company with senior government and industry stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build relationships across the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD),ONR, NAVSEA Warfare Centers, DARPA, other DoD S&T enterprise, and acquisition program offices, the Joint Staff, and the Military Departments, and represent Endurance Energy in meetings, working groups, and industry days

  • Track Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE), the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), and defense appropriations, and brief leadership on funding opportunities and timing risks

  • Engage Armed Services and Appropriations staff, draft talking points, white papers, and legislative asks, and manage outside lobbyists and coalitions

  • Work on programs and requirements, and support Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreements, Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) programs, Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) efforts, and teaming pursuits

  • Lead applications to Department of Defense (DoD) funding opportunities, from finding and qualifying solicitations through writing, submitting, and following up on proposals

  • Prepare presentations and briefing materials for senior leadership and external partners

  • Work with legal to keep all government engagement within lobbying, ethics, and procurement integrity rules

  • Own an annual Department of Defense (DoD) engagement plan and report regularly to executives and the board

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in government affairs, defense policy, or roles focused on the Department of Defense (DoD), with at least 5 years working directly with theONR, NAVSEA Warfare Centers, DARPA, other DoD S&T enterprise, and acquisition program offices or Military Departments

  • Working knowledge of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process, the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) and appropriations cycle, and Department of Defense (DoD) acquisition pathways, including the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreements, and Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) programs

  • Established relationships with Department of Defense (DoD), Service, or congressional defense stakeholders

  • Demonstrated ability to translate technical capabilities into policy and requirements language for non-technical audiences

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including senior-level briefings

  • Active Secret clearance or higher, or eligibility to obtain a Top Secret clearance

Preferred Skills

  • Master's degree in a related field, such as a Master of Public Administration (MPA), Master of Business Administration (MBA), or Juris Doctor (JD)

  • Prior service as a military officer, Department of Defense (DoD) civilian, or congressional staffer on a defense committee

  • Experience in energy, power systems, or critical infrastructure

  • Familiarity with Department of Defense (DoD) energy and installation programs, such as the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Energy, Installations, and Environment, the Environmental Security Technology Certification Program (ESTCP), the Strategic Environmental Research and Development Program (SERDP), or Service energy resilience offices

  • Experience supporting capture efforts for Department of Defense (DoD) contracts or other transactions

  • Active Top Secret clearance

Compensation, Benefits, & Perks

As a pre-revenue startup, Endurance Energy offers competitive base salaries and generous equity packages for full-time employees. Final base salary will be determined by an array of factors including internal equity, job-related knowledge, skills, and work experience.

A key aspect of our compensation philosophy is that value creation should be aligned with rewards. Right now this means equity is a significant portion of every full-time employee's compensation. As the company matures, there will be continued evolution and changes to the total rewards and total compensation package. What will always be true is that if we win, we win together. Equity is granted to every full-time employee as a meaningful piece of ownership. We believe the people building the company should share directly in the value they create.

In addition to a competitive base salary and equity, employees will receive all of our other great benefits and perks, including:

  • Benefits: Health, Dental, and Vision insurance coverage

  • Time Away: Flexible PTO including 12 paid company holidays

  • Global Fieldwork: Travel to fascinating deployment sites along oceanic ridges in locations like the Pacific Northwest, Hawaii, Iceland, Japan, New Zealand, and the Azores

  • Hands-on Experience: Participate in sea trials and deployment operations in partnership with leading oceanographic institutions

  • Cutting-edge Development: Work with technology that spans high-power electronics, marine systems, and clean energy

  • Impactful Work: Help solve one of the world's most pressing challenges

  • Dive Certification: Company-sponsored recreational dive certification

  • Other Perks: Access to the company boat, free meals and snacks, and the list goes on!

If you’re selected for consideration, a recruiter will be able to discuss in greater detail.

title: Internal Audit and Risk Management - Data Analytics & AI (Summer 2027 Internship - Washington, D.C.)
description:
Huron is a global consultancy that collaborates with clients to drive strategic growth, ignite innovation and navigate constant change. Through a combination of strategy, expertise and creativity, we help clients accelerate operational, digital and cultural transformation, enabling the change they need to own their future.

You'll help banks, asset management and insurance organizations own their future by helping them to transform and create new business models to meet changing customer needs and drive sustainability.

Join our team as the expert you are now and create your future.

About the Role
Interns will support internal audit and risk management engagements for financial institutions, with a strong focus on applying data analytics, artificial intelligence (AI), and model-driven approaches to enhance audit execution, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance. This role is designed for students who combine technical depth with an interest in audit, governance, and risk advisory.
Our Interns join us from a wide range of backgrounds and make an immediate impact working as part of a team committed to developing creative insights, implementing and designing processes, and driving tangible results. Interns receive training and coaching while gaining hands-on experience working independently and in team settings, building effective relationships, and delivering client solutions.

With a solution-oriented mindset, you will collaborate with team members to critically think and problem-solve while executing effective, technology-enabled audit and risk strategies. As an Intern, you will spend your summer working on client projects and participating in team culture initiatives and social events.

Role Focus
This role integrates internal audit, risk management, and regulatory advisory with advanced data analytics and AI, emphasizing the development and application of AI use cases and tools tailored to audit and risk management use cases within financial institutions.

Responsibilities May Include

  • Assisting with proposal development, including analytics- and AI-enabled approaches, budgeting, and project timelines for new business opportunities.
  • Supporting risk assessment and internal audit planning by:
    • Conducting research on client background, business activities, and key risks.
    • Assisting in internal audit risk assessments and development of audit plans.
    • Preparing materials for audit kick-off meetings and planning sessions.
    • Applying data analytics and AI techniques to support audit risk assessments and scoping decisions.
    • Assisting in the development of internal audit plans and preparation for client kick-off meetings.
  • Assisting in the end-to-end execution of internal audit projects, including:
    • Monitoring scope, risks, and issues.
    • Supporting audit fieldwork, documentation, and reporting activities.
  • Analyzing differences in policy management, governance structures, and control environments, identifying leading practices for financial institutions.
  • Monitoring changes in the regulatory environment and assessing their impact on the organization and client operations.
  • Supporting updates to the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework, including:
    • Major risk identification and maintenance of risk inventories.
    • Documentation of risk taxonomy and governance processes.
  • Supporting governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) initiatives, including:
    • Ensuring governance structures support effective risk and compliance management.
    • Assisting with governance training and education related to risk frameworks.
  • Supporting technology-enabled projects from a business and governance perspective, ensuring alignment with regulatory and operational requirements.
  • Coordinating with internal audit teams and client stakeholders to support project delivery.
  • Designing, developing, and testing data and AI to support audit and risk management use cases, such as:
    • Test case development, anomaly detection, and continuous auditing.
    • Risk indicator identification and monitoring.
    • Control effectiveness testing and trend analysis.
  • Developing and enhancing analytics tools and AI prompts/scripts to automate audit and risk processes.
  • Leveraging prominent AI frameworks and libraries to build, evaluate, and refine models used in audit and risk engagements.
  • Analyzing differences in policy management, control environment, and governance practices, identifying leading practices across financial institutions.
  • Monitoring changes in the regulatory environment and assessing their impact on audit scope, risk profiles, and compliance requirements.
  • Supporting updates to the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework, including major risk identification and maintenance of risk inventories.
  • Supporting governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) initiatives, including governance training and education related to risk frameworks.
  • Ensuring that technology-enabled audit and risk solutions improve business operations, audit quality, and regulatory compliance.

Hiring Requirements – Qualifications

  • Strong performance in a bachelor’s degree in a field related to this position or equivalent work experience obtained by Spring 2028:

title: Software Development Engineer, Network Fabric Engineering, MONA
description:
Do you like to use network and Unix systems engineering to deliver simple, sustainable, and repeatable solutions? Would you like to play a key role in driving the stability and sustainability of next-generation IP networks?

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Core Networking team is looking for a Software Development Engineer to join our Network Fabric Engineering (NFE) team. As a Software Development Engineer, you will be responsible for building software services to deploy and scale the Amazon networks that support AWS, customers, and other business units, across multiple global datacenters.

AWS Core Networking is focused on building Data Centers and the network that allows Data Centers to function efficiently. We own the solutions that allow racks to be aggregated and Data Centers to be interconnected. Core Networking's goal is to balance efficiency, performance and reliability to allow customers access to their applications and data.

Key job responsibilities
We are looking for an experienced Software Development Engineer with production quality software services experience.
- You are comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where delivery of new services and features is very rapid.
- The ideal candidate will demonstrate established software engineering expertise, having successfully developed and launched extensive distributed systems in collaboration with a team.
- You are adaptable, capable of excelling in a dynamic and entrepreneurial setting.
- You will be responsible for delivering high quality, extensible design and code.
- You are expected to have extensive background in network engineering and can troubleshoot network issues.
- You are expected to mentor and guide junior engineers.
- You are comfortable managing competing priorities and are able to bring order to ambiguous scenarios.
- You identify and implement optimizations for performance, scalability, and efficiency. Maturity, impeccable judgment, and the ability to influence and lead are essential to success in this role.
- You are data-driven and analytical.
- You have the ability to communicate clearly and effectively, both in writing and verbally, across organizations.


A day in the life
• Work in a 24x7 team on call rotation, with ability to drive into workplace for critical events/needs.
• Manage customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure.
• Sit at the computer during scheduled work hours with appropriate breaks while maintaining a high level of alertness and attention to detail.
• Travel to data center/network sites and Amazon/customer offices as needed.

About the team
AWS NFE (Network Fabric Engineering) owns datacenter network services that provide unconstrained connectivity to our customers, such as EC2, EBS, S3 and Amazon CDO Services. They own the networks internal to the datacenters end to end, including scaling and operational functions, for both traditional datacenters. They also own newer AWS offerings such as Outposts and Local Zones.

title: AI Deployment Manager
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

AI DEPLOYMENT MANAGER

As an AI Deployment Manager (ADM) at SpaceXSI, you'll own the post-sale journey for a portfolio of enterprise customers, driving adoption, retention, and expansion. You'll help engineering organizations successfully roll out SpaceXSI and evolve how they work with AI. You'll operate at the center of each account, partnering with developers, admins, and executives while working closely with Sales, Field Engineering, Product, and Support. You'll shape rollout strategy and influence SpaceXSI's roadmap priorities through customer insight.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Manage a book of business with our largest enterprise customers in the life sciences segment, owning the long-term success of each account

  • Engage CTO / VP / SVP Engineering stakeholders to demonstrate ROI and guide AI-driven organizational change

  • Lead enterprise rollouts end-to-end: onboarding, enablement, internal champions, and scaled adoption

  • Turn high-impact use cases into durable, repeatable workflows across teams

  • Monitor account health and usage data to drive renewals and expansion with AEs

  • Represent the customer internally, synthesizing feedback and influencing product priorities

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience in a customer-facing role at the intersection of business and technology

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Thrives in customer-facing roles

  • Experience working at the intersection of business and technology and thriving in customer-facing roles

  • Able to translate customer needs into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes

  • Understand modern engineering orgs, the SDLC, developer workflows, and tool adoption

  • Communicate comfortably with both developers and senior executives

  • Analytical and operational, using data to prioritize and drive action

  • Already a power user of Grok, Grok Build, Grok Bot, or Grok APIs (or modern AI tools for knowledge work and coding) with strong opinions about what great looks like (big plus)

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Remote but must be willing to travel to customer onsites as needed

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

The expected annual base salary range for this role is $164,500 - $200,000. This role is also eligible for sales commissions or bonuses, with an annual on-target earnings (OTE) range of $235,000 - $280,000. OTE includes base salary plus target incentive compensation, assuming 100% achievement of applicable performance targets. Actual incentive earnings depend on performance and the terms of the applicable plan.

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

title: Materials Research Department (MRD) Summer 2027 Intern
description:
Overview

Who we are

Collaborative. Respectful. A place to dream and do. These are just a few words that describe what life is like at Toyota. As one of the world’s most admired brands, Toyota is growing and leading the future of mobility through innovative, high-quality solutions designed to enhance lives and delight those we serve. You should not apply for this role if you will require Toyota to assist with immigration support or sponsorship now or in the future.


R&D Overview:

At Toyota Research and Development (R&D), we’re working to build a future where everyone has the freedom to move, with a focus on vehicle design and development, procurement, supplier engineering development, mobility, safety, and advanced research. Centered in Ann Arbor, Michigan, Toyota R&D has some of the brightest thinkers from across America dedicated to building the future of mobility where everyone can live more safely and comfortably.


Who we’re looking for:

As an intern with the Materials Research Department (MRD) within Toyota Research Institute of North America (TRINA), you will support projects that align with both departmental objectives and your personal development goals. You will contribute to in-house lab automation development and our collaboration project to implement high-throughput experimentation capabilities that accelerate materials research.


In this role, you will work alongside MRD researchers to help design and develop an automated experimental setup for polymer synthesis, including reagent mixing, heating, and real-time status monitoring. You will help program and control the setup to achieve desired synthesis conditions using data acquisition (DAQ) and control platforms, such as Raspberry Pi, LabJack, or similar systems. Your responsibilities will also include implementing appropriate safety features and safeguards to support safe and reliable operation.


You’ll work in a collaborative team environment to deliver meaningful contributions to the organization. This opportunity is ideal for a student interested in combining hands-on laboratory work with programming, instrumentation, and automation to advance materials research. Additionally, you will be paired with a non-technical mentor and have opportunities to participate in networking and professional development activities throughout your co-op term.


What you bring:

  • Must be 18 years of age or older
  • Minimum GPA of 3.0 or higher
  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Controls, Computer/Data Science, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Applied Physics, Automotive Engineering, or a closely related field


Belonging at Toyota


Our success begins and ends with our people. We embrace all perspectives and value unique human experiences. Respect for all is our North Star.

title: Product Designer , Customer Service Design
description:
The Customer Service Innovation Lab (CSIL) is a new team inside Amazon Customer Service. Its mission is to challenge the status quo and shape the future of the customer experience industry. We're looking for a Designer to join a Pioneering Pod and help turn real customer and contact handler insights into tested solutions, fast. You will observe Amazon Customer experiences daily, and that will shape everything you design. You'll work with a Senior Designer and cross-functional partners, own design for features and workstreams, and build prototypes that help the team decide what to do next. This role suits a curious designer who likes working hands-on with users, enjoys fast iteration, and wants to help invent what customer service looks like next.

Key job responsibilities
- Learn from customers every day: listen to contacts, observe customer journeys, and turn what you see into design opportunities.
- Bring fresh thinking: question "the way it's always been done" and suggest new approaches to the customer experience.
- Own design for defined workstreams within lab initiatives, from discovery through interaction design, prototyping and handoff.
- Work directly with contact handlers through observation, co-design sessions and quick usability tests.
- Build interactive prototypes quickly, including AI-powered experiences, to test ideas in days.
- Partner with PMs and engineers to scope MVPs, weigh trade-offs, and deliver designs that are ready to build.
- Design inclusively: apply accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 AA) and responsible-AI patterns.
- Share your work: present concepts and test results in pod reviews and lab demos.
- Use and add to the design system: reuse CS-UX patterns, and suggest new ones when lab work proves them out.

About the team
This team is comprised of small, cross-functional Pioneering Pods who work right next to our contact handlers, hearing the voice of the customer and watching real customer experiences every day. They prototype solutions in days instead of quarters and prove what works before it scales across the CS network.

title: Sr. Technical Product Manager, Prime Video Commerce Personalization and Member Experience
description:
Come build the future of entertainment with us. Are you interested in shaping the future of movies and television? Do you want to define the next
generation of how and what Amazon customers are watching?

Prime Video is a premium streaming service that offers customers a vast collection of TV shows and
movies — all with the ease of finding what they love to watch in one place. We offer customers thousands of popular movies and TV shows from Originals and Exclusive content to exciting live sports events. We also offer our members the opportunity to subscribe to add-on channels which they can cancel at anytime and to rent or buy new release movies and TV box sets on the Prime Video Store. Prime Video is a fast-paced, growth business — available in over 240 countries and territories worldwide. The team works in a dynamic environment where innovating on behalf of our customers is at the heart of everything we do. If this sounds exciting to you, please read on.

Hundreds of millions of customers open Prime Video every week. They trust us to help them find something great to watch. Increasingly, they expect us to help them discover title offers, channel and bundle subscriptions that match their interests.

Today, we break that trust in small but compounding ways. A customer declines an offer and sees it again minutes later. A new subscriber gets upsells before finding a show they love. A loyal viewer showing signs of leaving receives a generic message that ignores everything they have ever watched.

We are hiring a Sr. PMT to own Commerce Personalization for Prime Video. You will build the intelligence that makes every commerce interaction feel like it comes from a service that actually knows you.

This is a build-and-scale role. You will define what "right offer, right moment, right customer" means at Prime Video scale. You will ship systems that remember what customers have told us, respect their journey stage, and earn the right to make a recommendation. You will prove — through measurable customer outcomes — that respecting customer drives better business results than pressuring them.

Key job responsibilities
Own the customer problem end-to-end. Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Commerce Personalization across all Prime Video surfaces — homepage, detail pages, checkout, notifications, and partner storefronts.

Eliminate the contradictions customers experience today. Build coordinated intelligence, so a declined offer stays declined, at-risk customers get content before commerce, and new subscribers aren't treated like conversion targets. Define how we measure success and how it impacts our long-term success.

Crack problems others haven't, drive adoption at scale enabling Partner content discovery for the growing number of channels across 30+ countries. Personalized offer timing that converts because it's welcome

Ship fast, prove impact continuously. Start with the most painful customer contradiction and fix it. Every phase delivers measurable improvement — reduced repetition, better timing, higher engagement among at-risk segments. Build conviction through results.

Work backward from customers to technology. Partner with Applied Science and ML Engineering on reinforcement learning, multi-objective optimization, and unified customer representations — always in service of a specific customer outcome.

Drive organizational alignment. Get multiple teams to optimize shared customer outcomes over local metrics. Win this argument with evidence, not authority.

About the team
PV Commerce Personalization & Member Experience sits at the intersection of Prime Video's content experience and its commerce engine. We own the models, systems, and product experiences that determine which customers see which offers, when, and how. Our production models — including offer propensity, churn prediction, subscription ranking, and cross-offer optimization — serve decisions across every Prime Video commerce surface. We are evolving from siloed model optimization to a unified system that coordinates across the full customer journey. We are a product development team that partners closely with cross-functional teams across Prime Video to deliver customer and partner value.

title: Brewer - The Plant
description:
SUMMARY

The brewer position is full time (4x 10 hour shifts), Monday through Thursday or Tuesday through Friday at our Castroville Production Facility known as ‘The Plant’. This is a rotational position that will require an extensive period of training across all disciplines of our operation. Brewers will be trained to brew on our 50 bbl BrauKon brewhouse, clean & sanitize fermenters, brite tanks and other cellar equipment, and execute transfers of green beer through our centrifuge; learning and mastering the process from start to finish. The position will also support all packaging operations, with training on all packaging equipment, including the Krones filler and the Lambrechts keg racker. Upon completion of training, Brewers will spend each day of the work week under one area of operations - be it brewing, cellar, or packaging operations. This non-exempt hourly position will report directly to our Director of Brewing Operations.


DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Wort Production (1-2 days / week):
    • Following the automation protocol of BrauKon wort production, from grain management and handling to step mashing, decoction and cereal mashing, lautering, adding hops and other ingredients to the kettle, and casting out wort to fermenter.
    • Recording all applicable gravities, pH, temperatures, and other requested parameters and maintain required spreadsheets with wort data points taken throughout the process.
    • Maintaining sanitary working conditions and equipment at all times
    • Assist with harvesting yeast and performing pitch calculations.
    • Milling specialty malt and organizing malt in grist handling room; super sack management, cleanliness of malt area.
    • Pitching yeast, enzymes, zinc, and hops.
    • Inspecting and verifying cellar operations to related tanks. (E.g. Ensuring FVs have been cleaned and sanitized to protocol before knock out).
    • Consistently communicating status of daily brews with other brewers, ensuring good communication.
  • Cellar Tech (1-2 days / week )
    • Execute CIP of Fermenter vessels and brite tanks; Perform cleaning, sanitation, and CO2 purging.
    • Complete dry hopping, fruiting, and other dosing on beer throughout various stages of the cellaring.
    • Transfer, fine, and centrifuge product.
    • Maintain cleanliness and sanitation of all brewery equipment & parts, including cellar floors, drains, and tank exteriors.
    • Monitor the quality of the product: temperature, gravity, pH, VDK levels, and carbonation on all fermentation vessels and BBTs. Alerts the head brewer and QA/QC manager of any issues or concerns.
    • Assist with accurately harvesting yeast and performing pitch calculations.
  • Packaging Tech (1-2 days / week )
    • Operate the Krones filler; CIP, accept product, fill and seam cans, troubleshoot the in and outfeed.
    • Operate up and downstream equipment on the packaging line, including the Depalletizer, Labeler, Pak-Tech applicators and DMM tray packer.
    • Operate the Lambrecht keg racker - washing and cleaning kegs, filling kegs and troubleshooting.
    • Clean and sanitize all packaging equipment, floors and maintain an organized work environment.


SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

  • 21+ years of age
  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required; formal brewing education or a college degree preferred
  • 1-2 years of professional brewing experience required
  • Strong understanding of the brewing process
  • Forklift certified or ability to undergo certification training
  • Team player that also works well independently
  • Excellent verbal communication skills
  • High attention to detail with a focus on quality
  • Strong problem solving skills
  • Professional, courteous, and embodies the hospitality that we stand for as a company
  • Adaptable with the ability to prioritize tasks
  • Ability and desire to work in a fast-paced environment with a growing company
  • Passion for beer, enthusiastic about the process, and a desire to learn


PHYSICAL & MENTAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Able to stand, walk, and be on your feet for prolonged periods
  • Repetitive motion of the wrists, hands, and fingers
  • Able to maneuver on uneven ground
  • Able to read and follow written English instructions
  • Able to regularly twist, turn, kneel, climb, stoop, bend, and crawl on occasion
  • Able to lift and carry supplies and equipment weighing up to 50+ pounds on occasion and 25 pounds regularly using appropriate techniques and tools
  • Able to maneuver packages of any weight above 75 pounds with appropriate equipment and/or assistance
  • Able to safely navigate crowded spaces
  • Able to work in indoor and outdoor production environments which may be loud, slick, humid, cold, and hot with moderate noise and occasionally slippery floors with reasonable safety accommodations
  • Work safely with chemicals with reasonable safety accommodations

description:

As Senior Director, Platform Governance & Compliance, you will set the governance, risk, and compliance strategy for the FICO platform and serve as its credentialed authority on platform administration, access controls, and auditability across enterprise deployments. As a hands-on leader, you will own the governance product vision and FICO’s regulatory posture, represent that strategy to executive leadership, customers, regulators and auditors, and build the team that executes it.


What You'll Contribute


  • Own and evolve the platform's governance product strategy across its three pillars - Governance, Control, and Administration - aligning with business goals, customer needs, and the evolving regulatory landscape, with particular emphasis on the financial services risk and regulatory environment our platform operates within.
  • Champion the three-part controls model - prevent it, decide it, prove it stays right - and drive enterprise-wide adoption across platform services and leadership stakeholders.
  • Act as the primary bridge to C-suite, legal, and risk stakeholders - keeping governance conversations productive and release schedules on track.
  • Represent governance and compliance capabilities directly in strategic customer engagements, vendor risk assessments, and security questionnaires at the executive level - with credibility that resonates with financial services customers.
  • Set and defend the risk-adjusted prioritization framework (e.g., RICE, WSJF) that balances commercial growth against compliance mandates and regulatory exposure - the final decision-maker on trade-offs between the two.
  • Manage and mentor the Platform Governance & Compliance team, setting priorities and reviewing execution quality across PRDs, epics, and audit-readiness work.
  • Bring working fluency in financial services requirements (e.g., GLBA, model risk management practices) to guide platform strategy - engaging directly with regulators and auditors when needed.
  • Define the KPIs that measure governance, control, and administration effectiveness at the platform level, and report on them to executive leadership.

What we’re Seeking


  • In-depth experience in Platform Product Management or Governance/Compliance leadership, with substantial expertise in Financial Services (banking, lending, credit decisioning, or consumer finance) required; additional experience within Enterprise SaaS, Security, Cloud Infrastructure, or other regulated industries (HealthTech, GovTech) a plus.
  • Demonstrated track record shaping governance strategy within financial services or another regulated industry.
  • A recognized, credentialed name in the governance, compliance, or financial-regulatory community - established through public speaking, published thought leadership, regulatory or industry board participation, or prior senior regulatory/executive roles — bringing immediate external credibility to the position.
  • Executive presence: proven ability to represent governance strategy to C-suite, boards, and customers.
  • Strong grounding in identity and security architecture (RBAC/ABAC, MFA, SSO, encryption standards) sufficient to set strategy and evaluate team output, though day-to-day technical execution sits with the Director.
  • Relevant industry credentials (e.g., CISSP, CIPP, CRCM) are a plus, though not required.
  • Extensive experience in building or mentoring product management teams.

description:

What will your job look like?

The Mobility Assessment Evaluator (MAE) is responsible for reviewing ADA paratransit application materials, supplemental intake and professional verification forms, conducting in-person interviews for applicants, and performing functional assessments with applicants to determine eligibility for ADA paratransit service. The Mobility Assessment Evaluator (MAE) is also responsible for maintaining accurate documentation and providing final eligibility determinations to the Client.


This position sits in our Phoenix, AZ office working Mon-Fri. Hours of operations are 8am-5pm.

  • Determines final eligibility based upon the application, interview, functional assessment and any supplemental information

Experience, Education & Certifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Services, Rehabilitation, Ancillary Health Care Profession, or a related field
  • Willing to accept relevant experience and specialized certifications in lieu of a Bachelor’s degree depending upon contract specifications (Certifications can include: COTA, OT, PT)
  • 3+ years of professional experience working with individuals with disabilities
  • Experience and knowledge with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) regulations and sensitivity to issues relating to people with disabilities and older adults
  • Related experience with regard to the functional assessment of individuals with disabilities along with experience working with individuals with disabilities

Skills:

description:
Do you want to own the latest technology, solve new problems, and have the ability to see the impact of your successes?

Amazon is growing, and we need SDEs who move fast, are capable of breaking down and solving difficult problems, and have a strong will to get things done. SDEs at Amazon work on real-world problems on a global scale, own their systems end to end, and build technology that impacts hundreds of millions of customers around the world.

The AI Authoring team builds tools and agents that help service teams create, update, and validate AWS documentation used by millions of builders. As an SDE on the team, you'll own features from working backwards with customers through design, implementation, deployment, and operations, using AWS services for serverless compute, data, and GenAI. You'll work in a fast-moving space where practical, maintainable solutions matter more than novelty. - Design and deliver AI-powered features for AWS documentation authoring, from working backwards with customers through deployment and operations.
- Write high-quality, well-tested code that meets the Amazon Code Bar, using AI coding tools with judgment and owning the result.
- Build evaluations and guardrails that measure and improve the accuracy of AI-generated content.
- Measure whether the features you ship improve documentation quality and authoring speed for service teams.
- Design solutions to difficult problems, seeking guidance to align with the team's long-term architecture.
- Balance new feature work against operational excellence, and eliminate the root causes of failures.
- Document how your software is built, tested, operated, and secured, and train new team members on it.
- Give meaningful code-review feedback and mentor engineers on your team.
- Evaluate emerging GenAI approaches and recommend which ones the team should adopt.

A day in the life
You'll design and build features, write code with unit and integration tests, and review your teammates' designs and code. You'll take part in on-call, finding and fixing the root causes of issues, and you'll refactor and improve the systems you work on. You'll work with product managers and service teams to understand customer needs, contribute to team planning, and help new team members get up to speed. You'll break problems into smaller pieces and deliver incrementally. You'll use AI development tools every day and help the team learn where they work well and where they don't.

About the team
TCX Engineering builds customer-facing experiences to deliver technical documentation for AWS. We innovate, research, experiment, and collaborate with product managers to understand our customers' needs. We partner with AWS service teams to learn the inner workings of their services so that we can influence design and the customer experience. We are a catalyst in the successful adoption and implementation of AWS services. Within TCX Engineering, the AI Authoring team applies GenAI to the authoring workflow itself, helping service teams produce accurate documentation faster.

As a senior vendor manager, you will report to the head of vendor management and be responsible for leading a team of vendor managers and developing relationships with several of our key vendors and partners. You will work with Brazilian and global vendors to drive all aspects of terms improvements, which includes analysis and projections, as well as direct negotiations with decision makers in local vendors. Additionally, you will increase product category sales, by driving store marketing promotions, negotiating partners to improve selection, and reacting to industry-related economic trends.
You will have excellent verbal and written communication, the ability to analyze and communicate complex terms and margin structure and work well across other teams including Finance and Inventory Management. Candidates who are organized, flexible, creative, analytical, and able to drive negotiations through completion will be highly appreciated. Strong ownership values, a real passion for innovation, and hustle are also key to succeed in this position.
If you are passionate about e-commerce and career growth, this opportunity with Amazon.com.br is for you!

Key job responsibilities
Retail Managers focus on and act at the intersection of customers, vendors, and functional teams:

* CUSTOMERS: They rely on specialized teams for customer and category information and insights, and works with and influences other teams to get the category-specific customer needs addressed. The Retail Manager is responsible to hold category-specific knowledge about customers and their needs, emerging product trends and the market segment evolution, and new business opportunities.

*VENDORS: RM are the ultimate owners of the vendor relationship, with a direct focus on the top vendors that drive the vast majority of sales. They are directly responsible for auditing and escalating performance, improving overall terms and cost structures of the relationship by means of negotiation, and for developing long term partnerships with new and existing vendors to drive topline and selection fueling category growth.

*CENTRAL AND FUNCTIONAL TEAMS: As a business owner, the RM represents customer and business needs in interaction with central teams, projects and initiatives.The Retail Manager drives central teams for the evolution of customer-facing and internal systems to improve the customer experience from the category perspective. At the same time, they implements centrally driven initiatives within the category to drive CX or cost improvements, even more important prioritize based on impact and potential tradeoffs, and if need be pushing back on selected initiatives.

A day in the life
Retail Managers are owners of the Retail business. Either for subcategories or subgroup of vendors they own the respective business end-to-end including the entire P&L, from topline down to free cash flow. They manage inputs by driving selection, securing great prices and increasing convenience/speed to accelerate Amazon’s flywheel. While they focus their activities on our most strategically relevant vendors and holdouts, they audit and escalate the performance of lower tiered vendors.

title: Frontend Engineer II, Ground Control Console
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, built to deliver fast, reliable broadband to customers and communities around the world, including places traditional networks don't reach.

As a Frontend Engineer on the Leo Ground Control Console team, you'll build the web platform that Leo's engineers and operators use every day to run the constellation. That includes mission operations, network health, satellite and ground systems, and the leadership views that show how the network is performing. You'll own features end to end, from design through production, and see them used by the people flying and operating the network.

What you'll do
- Build and evolve a shared frontend platform that operator and leadership dashboards are built on: common components, charts, maps, tables, navigation, and mobile-friendly layouts, so every team ships a consistent, fast experience.
- Make operational tools fast and dependable at fleet scale. Profile and remove performance bottlenecks, design data-heavy views that stay responsive, and harden the platform against real-world failure modes.
- Instrument what you build. Use real-user monitoring and usage data to find where operators struggle, fix it, and measure the improvement.
- Work directly with engineering teams across ground and space systems to turn complex mission workflows into clear, easy-to-use tools.
- Raise the bar on engineering practice: shared design standards, automated code review, test and release tooling, and AI-assisted development workflows that help a small team move quickly without sacrificing quality.
- Support high-stakes moments such as launches, on-orbit operations and operational rehearsals, where the tools have to just work.

About you
You care about craft and about the people who use what you build. You're comfortable owning ambiguous problems, balancing several priorities at once, and staying calm under pressure. You have deep frontend engineering skills, enjoy making complex systems understandable, and like turning data into decisions. Experience with design systems, performance tuning or observability is a plus. Familiarity with space or network systems is welcome but not required; you'll learn the domain here.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

About the team
The Leo Ground Control Console team owns the operational tooling used across Amazon Leo, on the ground and in orbit. We build a shared platform that is scalable, reliable, adaptable and fast, so every team at Leo can deliver tools their users rely on. We're a small, high-ownership team that ships quickly, measures its impact, and invests in the tools and practices that make the whole organization more productive.

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, test and operate features end to end in the shared web platform behind Amazon Leo's operator and leadership tools, from design through production support.
- Build reusable components and patterns (tables, charts, maps, navigation, layouts and mobile views) that many teams adopt, and keep them consistent, accessible and well documented.
- Own the performance and reliability of data-heavy applications: measure real-user experience, find and fix bottlenecks, and make tools resilient to slow or failing dependencies.
- Add usage and error telemetry to what you ship, and use the data to prioritize improvements and show their impact.
- Partner with engineers, operators and product owners across ground and space systems to understand mission workflows and turn them into clear, efficient tools.
- Write high-quality, well-tested code, review others' changes, and help define the team's frontend standards, design guidelines and automated quality checks.
- Improve developer productivity through better tooling, CI/CD, test automation and AI-assisted development workflows.
- Participate in on-call and support launches, on-orbit operations and operational rehearsals, where the tools have to just work.

title: Global Head of Architecture
description:
Build the future of AI and data with us

Datatonic is a leading Google Cloud partner specialising in data and AI. We help organisations design, build and operate production AI systems, from governed data foundations and machine learning platforms to generative AI applications and agentic workflows. Our teams combine Google Cloud, software engineering, machine learning, data engineering and analytics expertise with the consulting skills needed to turn complex business requirements into reliable products.

Your mission

As Architecture Lead, you will be a hands-on Cloud Architect who also leads Datatonic's team of architects. You will design and build cloud, data and application estates yourself, while setting the standards, growing the people and owning the quality of architecture across our client work.

You will split your time between three things: delivering architecture on our most complex engagements, leading and developing a team of architects, and representing Datatonic as a technical authority with clients and in pre-sales.

What you'll do

Hands-on architecture

  • Target architecture: Design and lead target architectures across cloud, data and application estates on Google Cloud, covering the platforms and the systems that run on them.

  • Hands-on build: Stay close to the code. Prototype, write infrastructure as code, review pull requests and unblock engineering teams on hard technical problems.

  • Systems design: Own boundaries, failure modes, security, cost, operability and how each design evolves over time.

  • Trade-off ownership: Resolve architectural trade-offs across Platform, Data, Analytics, AI, Software and UX.

  • Delivery governance: Act as design authority on our most complex engagements, making sure what we ship is secure, reliable and maintainable.

Leading the architecture team

  • People leadership: Line manage and develop a team of architects, including career conversations, performance reviews and growth plans.

  • Mentorship: Coach architects and discipline leads while leaving delivery ownership with them.

  • Standards and patterns: Set architecture standards, reference patterns and decision-record practices used across projects and regions.

  • Capability building: Grow architecture capability through hiring, training, communities of practice and design reviews.

  • Staffing: Work with delivery leadership to match architects to engagements.

Clients and market

  • Pre-sales: Shape solution architecture, estimates and proposals, especially where estate design carries the risk.

  • Client leadership: Build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders, from engineering leads to CTOs.

  • Thought leadership: Help shape service propositions and represent Datatonic as a technical authority at events and with Google Cloud.

Working with agents

You will use agents throughout engineering delivery and maintain the agents that support the architecture discipline, including their versioning, evaluation, operation and continuous improvement. This covers agents for option analysis, decision-record drafts, consistency checks against established patterns, and initial threat and cost assessments.

What you'll bring

  • Cloud architecture depth: Extensive hands-on experience designing and building production systems on Google Cloud (or AWS/Azure with a strong interest in GCP).

  • Engineering foundation: Proven depth in at least one engineering discipline (platform, data, software or ML engineering) at Senior 2 / L5 or above.

  • Demonstrated breadth: Evidence of systems design across disciplines, including networking, security, IAM, data platforms and application architecture.

  • Hands-on skills: Comfortable with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform), CI/CD, containers and Kubernetes, and at least one programming language such as Python.

  • Team leadership: Experience leading, mentoring or line managing engineers or architects, and raising the bar for a whole team.

  • Client leadership: Client-facing architecture leadership with senior stakeholders, including pre-sales and solution shaping.

  • Communication: Ability to explain complex trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, in writing and in person.

Bonus points if you have

  • Google Cloud certifications: Professional Cloud Architect or similar.

  • Complex estates: Experience with multi-cloud, hybrid or complex integration environments.

  • Architecture methods: Experience applying formal architecture methods (e.g. TOGAF) in complex delivery environments.

  • AI and data platforms: Experience architecting ML platforms, generative AI applications or agentic systems in production.

  • Consultancy background: Experience in a consultancy or professional services environment.

What's in it for you?

We believe in empowering our team to thrive, with benefits including:

  • Holiday: 25 days plus bank holidays.

  • Health perks: Private health insurance (Vitality Health) and Smart Health Services.

  • Fitness and wellbeing: 50% gym membership discounts (Nuffield Health, Virgin Active, Pure Gym).

  • Hybrid model: Two to three days in the office, with a WFH allowance to keep you comfortable.

  • Learning and growth: Dedicated learning budgets and access to platforms like Udemy.

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment after probation. 3% employer contributions, rising 1% per year of service to a maximum of 10%.

  • Life insurance: Three times your base salary.

  • Income protection: Up to 75% of base salary, for up to two years.

  • Schemes: Cycle to Work and Tech schemes.

Why Datatonic?

Join us to work alongside AI enthusiasts and data experts who are shaping tomorrow. Innovation is central to our work, from the technology we use to the way we solve client problems. If you are ready to lead architecture at the forefront of data and AI, we would like to hear from you.

Apply now and take your career to the next level.

title: Product Designer , Customer Service Design
description:
The Customer Service Innovation Lab (CSIL) is a new team inside Amazon Customer Service (CS). Its mission is to challenge the status quo and shape the future of the customer experience industry. We're looking for a Designer to join a Pioneering Pod and help turn real customer and contact handler insights into tested solutions, fast. You will observe Amazon Customer experiences daily, and that will shape everything you design. You'll work with a Senior Designer and cross-functional partners, own design for features and workstreams, and build prototypes that help the team decide what to do next. This role suits a curious designer who likes working hands-on with users, enjoys fast iteration, and wants to help invent what customer service looks like next.

Key job responsibilities
- Learn from customers every day: listen to contacts, observe customer journeys, and turn what you see into design opportunities.
- Bring fresh thinking: question "the way it's always been done" and suggest new approaches to the customer experience.
- Own design for defined workstreams within lab initiatives, from discovery through interaction design, prototyping and handoff.
- Work directly with contact handlers through observation, co-design sessions and quick usability tests.
- Build interactive prototypes quickly, including AI-powered experiences, to test ideas in days.
- Partner with PMs and engineers to scope MVPs, weigh trade-offs, and deliver designs that are ready to build.
- Design inclusively: apply accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 AA) and responsible-AI patterns.
- Share your work: present concepts and test results in pod reviews and lab demos.
- Use and add to the design system: reuse CS-UX patterns, and suggest new ones when lab work proves them out.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a design review where you present interaction concepts to your product and engineering partners, gathering feedback that sharpens direction. By midday you could be deep in prototyping a new flow, testing how an AI-powered feature feels in a customer's hands. You will regularly move between high-fidelity mockups, stakeholder conversations, and data analysis — balancing craft with collaboration to keep work moving toward launch.

About the team
This team is comprised of small, cross-functional Pioneering Pods who work right next to our contact handlers, hearing the voice of the customer and watching real customer experiences every day. They prototype solutions in days instead of quarters and prove what works before it scales across the CS network.

title: Security Engineer, GRC
description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

As a Security Engineer on the Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team, you’ll help build and scale programs that support commercial audits, federal compliance, security risk management, vendor risk, policy management, and customer trust. You’ll turn complex requirements into practical controls, reliable workflows, and measurable improvements while partnering across Security, Engineering, Legal, Privacy, and other teams. You’ll be expected to identify opportunities where AI can improve GRC workflows and turn useful experiments into practical, reliable solutions. Your work will help 1Password protect the people, businesses, and digital experiences that depend on secure access every day.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What we're looking for:

• Bring three or more years of experience in security, compliance, risk, audit, GRC, program management, or a related technical discipline.

• Manage moderately complex, cross-functional compliance or security initiatives with a high degree of organization, ownership, and follow-through.

• Apply one or more security or compliance frameworks, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, CMMC, FedRAMP, PCI DSS, or similar standards.

• Support FedRAMP or comparable federal compliance programs, ideally in a program management, project management, or cross-functional coordination capacity. Familiarity with authorization boundaries, assessment preparation, Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), continuous monitoring, Third-Party Assessment Organization (3PAO) coordination, or remediation is valuable.

• Translate framework requirements into clear control activities, policies, procedures, test cases, evidence requirements, and operational workflows.

• Work with GRC platforms such as Drata, Tines, Vanta, ServiceNow, Archer, LogicGate, Secureframe, or comparable tools, and use automation techniques such as APIs, scripts, webhooks, ticketing workflows, and cloud or identity integrations.

• Actively use AI in day-to-day work and show a clear trajectory toward building with it, including experimenting with or configuring AI-assisted workflows for GRC, security, risk, or compliance tasks. Understand the need for validation, human judgment, reliable controls, and appropriate review before relying on AI-generated outputs.

What you can expect:

• Manage GRC initiatives spanning commercial compliance, federal compliance, security risk, vendor risk, policy management, and customer trust.

• Support planning, assessment preparation, remediation, and continuous monitoring activities for FedRAMP, CMMC, NIST 800-53, and related programs.

• Partner with control owners, Security, Engineering, Legal, Privacy, auditors, assessors, and business stakeholders to gather evidence, track actions, and resolve gaps.

• Define and improve how evidence is generated, validated, mapped to requirements, stored, and traced to its source.

• Monitor control health, evidence freshness, configuration drift, exceptions, and remediation progress.

• Build or configure automated and AI-assisted workflows that reduce manual effort and improve the reliability of compliance and risk processes.

• Maintain project plans, action trackers, risk logs, documentation, and status updates while contributing to repeatable team practices and knowledge sharing.

USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $123,000 USD and $172,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $111,000 CAD and $155,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.


Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

We are searching for the best talent for an Experienced Scientist, Proteomics to be located in Cambridge, MA.


Purpose: Do you want to use your hard-earned skills and drive to make a difference in the lives of patients? Join the growing Discovery Proteomic Platforms (DPP) group within the Discovery Technologies and Molecular Pharmacology (DTMP) department of Therapeutics Discovery to apply groundbreaking approaches to high-scale proteomic analysis.

Be part of a motivated team deploying cutting-edge mass spectrometry technologies to tackle challenges in end-to-end drug discovery and development. Work across a leading multiomics organization to provide coordinated insights across a variety of 'omics layers.

This is a hands-on laboratory role, fit for a scientist who thrives at the bench and wants to grow in experimental design and scientific communication by working closely with senior scientists. With your help, we will drive development of medicines for our patients!


You will be responsible for:

  • Joining a team of wet lab scientists enabling proteomic impact across a wide variety of programs and therapeutic modalities.
  • Planning and performing wet lab proteomic activities supporting evaluation of therapeutic candidates.
  • Generating samples for proteomics analysis from multiple sources (immortalized cell lines, FFPE, fresh-frozen tissue, plasma/serum, etc.).
  • Maintaining multiple cell lines in both flasks and plates. Preparing assay plates and performing chemical treatments and perturbations.
  • Applying high-efficiency proteomics sample preparation methodologies across many experiment types (global proteomic profiling, immunoprecipitation, affinity, PTM analysis).
  • Operating and maintaining LC-MS instrumentation (Thermo Orbitrap Exploris/Eclipse/Astral, Bruker timsTOF; LC systems such as Vanquish Neo, Evosep One, UltiMate 3000), including daily/weekly maintenance, calibration, and troubleshooting.
  • Deploying automation-supported workflows for high-throughput sample prep using platforms such as Hamilton Microlab STAR, Tecan Fluent, AssayMAP Bravo, Beckman Biomek, or Dynamic Devices Lynx.
  • Ensuring QC and reproducibility, including system suitability checks, performance tracking, and SOP documentation.
  • Collaborating with colleagues within the proteomics group to drive proteomics experiments across the drug discovery portfolio.
  • Demonstrating creativity and applying novel approaches to solving scientific problems. Proposing novel and practical ideas aligned with scientific strategies and demands.

Education:

  • A Master's degree with 1+ years, or a Bachelor's degree with 3+ years, of proven experience in a proteomics laboratory setting (in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Biology, Molecular Biology, Pharmacology, or a related field).

Experience and Skills:

Required:

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience with mammalian cell culture and treatment.
  • Experience with label-free proteomics workflows and robust sample preparation techniques.
  • Strong planning and organizational skills with the ability to handle several projects at a time in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills working with diverse colleagues.

Preferred:

  • Experience with liquid chromatography (Thermo Vanquish Neo, EASY-nLC, UltiMate 3000, or Evosep One) and mass spectrometry (Thermo Exploris, Eclipse, Lumos, Astral, or Bruker timsTOF) instrumentation.
  • Experience with data processing suites such as Proteome Discoverer, MaxQuant, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, or Skyline.

title:
Senior Manager, Automation & Analytics

description:
Amazon Leo is building a low Earth orbit satellite constellation to bring fast, affordable connectivity to customers around the world. Direct to Device (D2D) extends Leo to standard mobile phones and devices: a fully regenerative fifth-generation (5G) mobile base station on each satellite, delivering service to standard handsets through mobile network operators (MNOs). D2D Software builds the embedded software that flies, the cloud and ground software that runs the service, and the platform that connects them. Our target is under a day from a defect being found to the fix deployed across the entire constellation, achieved by automating everything that a person would otherwise do by hand.

This role leads automation and analytics in Software Delivery & Business Ops, reporting to the Director, Software Delivery & Business Ops. It owns dashboards, business-review tooling, workflow automation, and delivery and efficiency analytics; the analytics and science lead and the DevOps technical program manager, with supplier delivery for DevOps tools, report here. Before anything is handed on, the bar is: every review derived from the systems of record. It hands off to its customers as follows: dashboards and analytics to all teams.

What the team needs to achieve
• Every review derived from the systems of record.
• Hand-offs that meet their service level: dashboards and analytics to all teams.
• Measured, rising capability and efficiency of the team, with manual work falling release over release.

How the team is measured
• Business-review content derived from the systems of record.
• Human time to prepare a business review.
• Manual repeated work per release.
• DevOps milestones and service levels met.

Key job responsibilities
• Own dashboards, business-review tooling, workflow automation, and delivery and efficiency analytics; the analytics and science lead and the DevOps technical program manager, with supplier delivery for DevOps tools, report here.
• Meet the bar before every hand-off: every review derived from the systems of record.
• Work directly with engineers in the boundary teams as partners, through agreed contracts and service levels.
• Automate everything a person would otherwise do twice.
• Hire, coach, and grow a small team, with clear expectations and career development for every member.
• Set the strategy and mechanisms for this area across the organization, and remove the bottlenecks that slow teams down.
• Own supplier delivery for this area: schedules, service levels, and escalation.
• Identify and mitigate risks before they become roadblocks, and escalate serious risks to senior leaders early.


This role leads a small team of automation engineers, data and analytics specialists, and the DevOps technical program manager. The team builds the automation and analytics that let a lean function run a large organization: dashboards, business-review tooling, workflow automation, and delivery and efficiency analytics. Through the DevOps technical program manager it also owns the handovers, milestones, service levels, and supplier delivery for DevOps & Release. It matters because status must be derived from the systems of record, not gathered by people, and efficiency must be measured to improve. Without it, business reviews are assembled by hand, status is stale, and the organization cannot see where its time goes.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


About the team
D2D Software is an evolving organization of many teams: Software Architecture & Specifications; Software Delivery & Business Ops; Software Integration, Verification & Reliability; DevOps & Release; Satellite Software Development; Ground Software Development; and Customer Software Engineering & Support. Each Director owns business outcomes: delivering the commitments, and the capability and efficiency of their teams. Teams work as internal customers and suppliers with agreed service levels, interfaces are agreed centrally while designs stay local, and engineers are expected to work directly with engineers across every boundary. Milestones are committed deadlines for delivery with quality, not gates to wait on, and every team runs on one toolchain and one system of record. Every measure is derived from the systems of record, never self-reported, and we improve release over release with a target of perfection.
