title: Mechanical Design Engineering Team Lead
description:
About pplwise

pplwise is a recruiting consultancy for fast-growing technology companies across Europe. Through Recruiting as a Service and Executive Search, we fill key roles for our clients, from start-ups to publicly listed companies. We are filling this position for our client Filics.

About our client: Filics

Filics is reinventing intralogistics with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that change how material moves. Its double-runner system makes Filics the first and only AMR that can drive through load carriers such as Euro pallets. This breaks with forklift logic and sets a new standard for efficiency. Filics is a small, hands-on team that solves hard problems with engineering excellence. Leadership goes to those who take initiative and consistently deliver. As Senior Mechanical Design Engineer (m/f/d) at Filics, you will lead the mechanical design of the robots as they move from prototype to series production.

About the role

This is an on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to engineering and assembly.

Filics builds its own robot hardware in-house: mechanics, electronics and software. Orders are growing, and the robots are moving from prototypes to series production. Designs that worked in the lab now need to be built reliably, at scale and at the right cost. The hardest problems often sit between disciplines: parts that work on their own can fail once they're assembled with the electronics.

The mechanical team has four engineers, most of them at the start of their careers, and they need someone who guides them every day. You'll be the technical lead for the mechanical side of the product and the counterpart to the electronics lead, so the current mechanical manager can focus on core R&D. Your time splits roughly evenly between hands-on engineering and technical leadership. You'll work closely with Electronics, Production, Procurement and the CTO, and you'll set the engineering habits while the team is still small.

What you'll do

  • Mentor the mechanical engineers day to day: help them make design decisions, set methods and keep projects focused

  • Design parts and assemblies in CAD, including tolerancing, and check every design for manufacturability and cost before it goes out

  • Lead testing and integration of mechanics and electronics, and solve the problems that only show once everything is assembled

  • Prioritise incoming work, follow up on progress and make the day-to-day technical calls on the mechanical side

  • Make the gated design process work in practice and run design reviews (safety, mechanics, electronics, manufacturability) before parts are integrated

  • Put design for manufacturing and design for cost in place: fewer, standardised parts and production methods that scale

  • Work with the electronics owner of each robot module from the first prototype on, and with Production on manufacturability and production jigs

  • Build and iterate prototypes based on customer and field feedback

About you

  • Several years of hands-on mechanical design in R&D at a company that develops and builds its own electromechanical products (e.g. power tools, home appliances, e-mobility, production machines, robotics, marine propulsion)

  • A proven record of taking an electromechanical product from prototype to series production (ideally 1,000+ units a year) on a fast development cycle of about a year, not a decade-long program

  • You still design hands-on in CAD, mainly metal parts and assemblies, with strong tolerancing skills (any CAD tool; Onshape is a plus)

  • You've applied design for manufacturing and design for cost, and cut cost through design: fewer parts, standard parts

  • At least two years of mentoring or technically guiding other engineers; a team-lead title isn't required

  • Experience testing and integrating mechanics with electronics

  • You've introduced processes, design reviews or engineering standards that helped a team deliver

  • You handle unclear requirements and break complex problems down so others can work on them

  • German is a plus, since production is mostly German-speaking

  • Bonus: GD&T and tolerance stack-ups, design of production jigs, or projects with motors, motor controllers or electronics

What Filics offers

  • A key role at an early stage: shape both the mechanical team and the product

  • Real ownership of the mechanical side, from first prototype to series production

  • A mix of hands-on engineering and leadership, with a path into team lead and engineering management as Filics grows

  • Fast design cycles driven by customer and field feedback

  • A small, high-caliber team with close collaboration across mechanics, electronics, software and production

  • Fast growth: one year at Filics teaches you what usually takes many years at a large company

  • An on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to Engineering and Assembly

Sound like you? Apply with your CV.

title: Senior Product Engineer
description:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

How we work

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 3, that looks like this.

What you'll be doing

  • Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

  • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

  • B2B

    • 25 days of non-working + Polish bank holidays

    • £5,000 GBP budget for Learning & Development

    • Mental Health Support and Therapy via Spectrum Life

    • Optional for you: access to Private Healthcare via Luxmed + Multisport (fully funded by yourself as B2B Contractor)

    • Top-spec laptop (MacOS or Windows)

  • Contract of Employment (UoP)

    • £5,000 GBP budget for Learning & Development

    • 26 days of holiday + Polish bank holidays

    • Company pension

    • Company Sick Pay for 10 days at 100% salary

    • Mental Health Support and Therapy via Spectrum Life

    • Monthly Wellbeing allowance via Juno

    • Private Healthcare Insurance via Luxmed

    • Multisport - Classic level

    • Top-spec work equipment (MacOS, Windows + additional monitors, mechanical keyboards etc)

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Lead Hirer Interview

  3. Live AI Skills Assessment

  4. Values Interview with the CPTO

  5. Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

- Earn trust with design, product, science, and engineering partners, demonstrating empathy, candor, and backbone through all levels of communication

A day in the life
- Taking a feature from a rough idea to production in days, not quarters

title: Lead Data Engineer
description:
What we’re all about.

It isn’t often you get to be part of a tech company that, since 2016, has been innovating the data analytics market in ways no-one else can. Our technology started out in FinTech, helping tackle serious criminal activity. Now, its potential is virtually limitless. Working at Quantexa isn't just intellectually stimulating. We’re a real team. Collaborating and constantly engineering better and better solutions. We’re ambitious, we think things through and we’re on a mission to discover just how far we can go. Nearly half of our colleagues come from an ethnic or religious minority background. We’re made up of people from 47 nationalities who speak over 20 languages. As a diverse mix of individuals, we make one big unstoppable team.

If our incredible culture sounds like you, we’d love you to join us.

The opportunity.

Our Quantexa Delivery team is all about bringing context to data. Lead Data Engineers are drivers within our fast-paced delivery teams, implementing Quantexa’s innovative technology for an ever-expanding list of domains including banking, insurance, government, healthcare. We are problem solvers, delivering sophisticated end-to-end big data solutions to our internal and external client stakeholders. As a central part of our team, you will experience opportunities beyond that of an engineer. You enjoy leading by example, guiding and mentoring data engineers to solve complex technical problems, sharing success with the team and taking pride in achieving milestones together. You share success with the team and take pride in the sum of its achievements. You will balance your time engaging with our business teams and clients to break down requirements into technical tasks, working hands-on as a programmer, and supporting the work of other engineers within a collaborative environment.

The work you do here will be impactful. The challenges we tackle are big, but they're also incredibly rewarding. Your leadership in managing, transforming, and cleansing high volume data help our clients solve business problems across a wide range of areas including fraud, financial crime, data management, risk and customer intelligence.

What you’ll be doing.

  • You will lead, support, and mentor a team of junior data engineers within an agile framework.

  • Write defensive, fault tolerant and efficient code for production level data processing systems.

  • You’ll configure and deploy Quantexa’s software using tools such as Spark, Hadoop, Scala, Elasticsearch, with our platform being hosted on both private and public virtual clouds, such as Google cloud, Microsoft Azure and Amazon.

  • You will be a trusted source of knowledge to your clients. You will articulate technical concepts to a non-technical audience helping them to make big decisions.

  • Collaborate with both our solution architects and our R&D engineers to champion solutions and standards for complex big data challenges. You proactively promote knowledge sharing and ensure best practice is followed.

What you’ll bring.

  • You’ll have a background in hands-on technical development, with at least five years of industry experience in a data engineering role or engineering equivalent, and at least 2 years of experience acting in a lead role within a data or software engineering team.

  • Proficiency in Scala, Java, Python, or a programming language associated with data engineering. Our primary language is Scala, but don’t worry if that’s not currently your strongest language, we believe that strong engineering principles are universal and transferrable.

  • You’ll have expertise building and deploying production level data processing batch systems maintained by application support teams. Importantly you’ll share an appreciation of what makes a high quality, operationally stable system and how to streamline all areas of development, release, and operations to achieve this.

  • Experience with a variety of modern development tooling (e.g. Git, Gradle, Nexus) and technologies supporting automation and DevOps (e.g. Jenkins, Docker and a little bit of good old Bash scripting). You’ll be familiar with developing within a version-controlled process that regularly makes use of these tools and technologies.

  • A strong technical communication ability with demonstrable experience of working in rapidly changing client environments.

  • Knowledge of testing libraries of common programming languages (such as ScalaTest or equivalent). Knows the difference between different test types (unit test, integration test) and can cite specific examples of what they have written themselves.

  • Candidates for this role must be eligible to obtain government security clearance.

Nice to haves.

  • Experience growing and up-skilling team members as a career mentor, technical line manager, or acting in an equivalent guidance role.

  • A passion for expanding the business – and leading initiatives to do so.

Our perks and quirks.

What makes you Q will help you to realize your full potential, flourish and enjoy what you do, while being recognized and rewarded with our broad range of benefits.

We offer:

  • Competitive salary & Company bonus

  • 30 days of annual leave, plus national holidays + your birthday off!

  • Regularly bench-marked salary rates

  • 5% of Employer Pension contribution

  • Life Insurance and Disability Cover

  • Comprehensive Statutory Healthcare & Family Leave Provisions

  • Well-being days

  • Volunteer Day off

  • Work from Home Equipment

  • Free Subscription to a meditation, relaxation and sleep app

  • Continuous Training and Development

  • Spend up to 2 months working outside of your country of employment over a rolling 12-month period with our ‘Work from Anywhere’ policy

  • Team Social Budget & Company-wide Socials

Our mission.

We have one mission. To help businesses grow. To make data easier. And to make the world a better place. We’re not a start-up. Not anymore. But we’ve not been around that long either. What we are is a collection of bright, passionate minds harnessing complexities and helping our clients and their communities. One culture, made of many. Heading in one direction – the future.

It’s all about you.

We want you to feel welcome, valued, and respected - because it’s your individuality and passion that make you Q. We see that, and we celebrate it. That’s why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment, continuously improving to ensure everyone belongs. Our recruitment process is designed to be inclusive and accessible. If you need any reasonable adjustments or accommodations, please let our Talent Acquisition Team know - we’re happy to assist.

No matter your race, beliefs, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, neurodiversity, or abilities—whoever you are—if you're a passionate, curious, and caring human eager to push the boundaries of what’s possible, we want to hear from you.

title: Solutions Architect - Australia
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SOLUTIONS ARCHITECT - AUSTRALIA

We're hiring Solution Architects to help the world's best engineering organizations figure out what AI-native software development actually looks like in production. This is a deeply technical, post-sale role embedded inside SpaceXSI's most strategic enterprise accounts. You'll work directly with engineering teams to roll out high-impact workflows, accelerate adoption, and help organizations fundamentally rethink how software gets built with AI. Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development: Roll out SpaceXSI across strategic engineering organizations; configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions; help developers integrate SpaceXSI into real production workflows, not isolated demos; drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams; identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly

  • Expand SpaceXSI Across the Organization: Identify where SpaceXSI should expand next inside the customer environment; help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption; design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups; partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale; work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments

  • Become a Trusted Technical Partner: Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders; lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions; advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy; coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress; help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves

  • Drive Real Customer Outcomes: Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact; connect SpaceXSI usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality; help customers communicate the value of SpaceXSI internally and build momentum for broader adoption; turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization

  • Help Make SpaceXSI Indispensable: Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness; monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on SpaceXSI over time; support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction; help customers build workflows they can't imagine operating without

  • Shape the Future of the Product: Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering; identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements; help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships; turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role such as Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • The ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

  • A strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

  • Strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

  • High ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

  • A passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willing to travel to customers

title: Engagement Manager, Professional Services, NAMER
description:

Are you passionate about helping organizations transform their businesses through cloud technology? Amazon Web Services (AWS) Professional Services is looking for an Engagement Manager to lead the delivery of complex cloud solution projects and serve as a trusted advisor to our customers. In this role, you will combine technical knowledge with project leadership to drive successful implementations of AWS-based solutions. You will bridge business requirements with technical realities, facilitate meaningful discussions across stakeholders, and ensure every engagement delivers measurable outcomes. If you are a collaborative problem-solver who thrives at the intersection of technology and business strategy, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead and manage the full lifecycle of cloud implementation and migration projects, creating engagement schedules, defining workstreams, and building executable roadmaps aligned to customer business outcomes.
- Bridge business requirements with technical solutions by distilling customer needs into clear technical requirements, decomposing complex problems, and making informed trade-off decisions that balance performance, scalability, and security.

- Facilitate release planning and enforce quality mechanisms across engagements, holding teams accountable for operational rigor including status reporting, documentation standards, and adherence to AWS frameworks.
- Build and maintain trusted customer relationships by understanding their strategic goals, communicating technical concepts to both technical and business audiences, and identifying opportunities to expand engagement scope.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a stand-up alongside your cross-functional project team, aligning priorities for the sprint and reviewing progress against customer milestones. Mid-day, you could be facilitating a working session with customer stakeholders to refine technical requirements and address emerging risks. In the afternoon, you might review engagement financials, update project documentation, or mentor a newer team member on delivery best practices. You will regularly collaborate with solutions architects, consultants, and partner teams to keep engagements on track and customers confident in their cloud journey.

About the team
AWS Professional Services is a global team of experts that helps customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network to execute enterprise cloud computing initiatives, providing assistance through a collection of offerings that help customers achieve specific outcomes related to cloud adoption. Our team values curiosity, continuous improvement, and an inclusive culture where every voice contributes to how we deliver for customers. Under the direction of the Supervisor/Manager, duties include all activities for creating a positive patient experience with nutrition services. Utilizing automated system, obtains patient’s menus; reviews choices with patients to ensure understanding and compliance to diet order. Responsible for delivery of meals: performs customer satisfaction rounds with patients after meal service and collects trays. Oversees nourishment kitchen stocking, rotating and sanitation. All guest rep services are performed in compliance with proper food handling techniques, infection control policies, and safety guidelines of the hospital and all regulatory agencies. Enhances the South Shore Hospital experience for patients, their families and visitors by providing appropriate hospitality and food services in a manner that reflects well on the hospital's reputation and image. Contributes to departmental patient satisfaction goals for excellence in all patient interactions. Works well with peers, contributes to a pleasant, professional, safe clean work environment.

$17.30 - $24.75

1. Visits patients, of all ages, daily; as assigned for menu selections. All visits are conducted in a manner that contributes to positive patient outcomes and enhances patient satisfaction.

a. Utilizes all resources available (current diet, missing menu, unit manager, etc.) to ensure every patient is visited for menu selections

b. Provides patients with overview of nutrition services, ensuring patients understand how meal service works

c. Facilitates a warm and friendly relationship with patients; creating memorable experiences intended to exceed patient expectations with food service. Reports any patient complaints to supervisor/manager and service recovery tools are utilized.

d. All department scripting is followed


2. Presents menus and assists with menu choices

a. Provides laminated menus; informs patient of physician ordered diet

b. Informs patient of physician ordered diet and asks if they have any other special dietary needs or food allergies

c. All meal items provided reflect review of patient's orders for diet restrictions, food allergies and texture modifications


3. Delivers patients meals and snacks

a. Follows department scripting; knocks, introduces self by name and department, and asks for permission to enter

b. Follows patient identification protocol; asks patient to state name, month, and day of birth to compare to each meal tray

c. Bedside tables are cleared and within reach for patient


4. Revisits all patients following meal service

a. Dirty trays are collected and truck returned to dish room within expected time frames

b. Patients are asked if there is anything else they need; if they are comfortable in the room and/or need anything cleaned

c. Environmental Services is notified of any room related issues

a. Follows proper patient identification policies

b. Demonstrates understanding of all patient care signage reflecting patients at risk - Falling Star, Suicide Precaution (black dot), Behavior issues, NPO, supervised, etc.

c. Demonstrates knowledge of Infection Control guidelines: Universal Precautions, Isolation specific signage, etc.

d. Follows department standards: does not engage in horseplay, posts wet floor signs as needed, reports faulty equipment


6. Identifies patients at nutritional risk or with special dietary needs

a. Menus are reviewed with patient for nutritional adequacy, cultural appropriateness and general satisfaction with items offered; is able to access Interpreter assistance and Culture vision as needed

b. Communicates any concerns or issues to Manager, Supervisor, Nutrition Coordinator or Dietitian

a. Hands are properly washed and/or sanitized. Before and After protocols are followed. Hairnets and gloves are worn whenever serving or working with food

b. Appearance conveys a professional image by adhering to department uniform policy and hospital dress code; only standard uniform is worn and is kept clean, neat, and free of tears

a. Inventories stock and restocks to established par levels

b. All stock is properly dated, rotated, and stored in proper locations

c. Refrigeration is kept free of spills

d. Condiment cabinets are neat, clean, and organized

e. Refrigerators, tray cabinets, microwaves and other equipment in kitchenettes that need detail cleaning are reported to manager or supervisor

a. Effectively utilizes systems: Outlook, Epic, CBORD, My Time, Healthstream, etc., manages/monitors own time card, monitors emails and tiger messages for communications

c. Completes all assigned mandatory education within expected time frames

d. Participates in continued learning and possess a willingness and ability to learn and utilize new technology and procedures that continue to develop in their role and throughout the organization.

e. Embraces technological advances that allow us to communicate information effectively and efficiently based on role.

title: Global Head of Architecture
description:
Build the future of AI and data with us

Datatonic is a leading Google Cloud partner specialising in data and AI. We help organisations design, build and operate production AI systems, from governed data foundations and machine learning platforms to generative AI applications and agentic workflows. Our teams combine Google Cloud, software engineering, machine learning, data engineering and analytics expertise with the consulting skills needed to turn complex business requirements into reliable products.

Your mission

As Architecture Lead, you will be a hands-on Cloud Architect who also leads Datatonic's team of architects. You will design and build cloud, data and application estates yourself, while setting the standards, growing the people and owning the quality of architecture across our client work.

You will split your time between three things: delivering architecture on our most complex engagements, leading and developing a team of architects, and representing Datatonic as a technical authority with clients and in pre-sales.

What you'll do

Hands-on architecture

  • Target architecture: Design and lead target architectures across cloud, data and application estates on Google Cloud, covering the platforms and the systems that run on them.

  • Hands-on build: Stay close to the code. Prototype, write infrastructure as code, review pull requests and unblock engineering teams on hard technical problems.

  • Systems design: Own boundaries, failure modes, security, cost, operability and how each design evolves over time.

  • Trade-off ownership: Resolve architectural trade-offs across Platform, Data, Analytics, AI, Software and UX.

  • Delivery governance: Act as design authority on our most complex engagements, making sure what we ship is secure, reliable and maintainable.

Leading the architecture team

  • People leadership: Line manage and develop a team of architects, including career conversations, performance reviews and growth plans.

  • Mentorship: Coach architects and discipline leads while leaving delivery ownership with them.

  • Standards and patterns: Set architecture standards, reference patterns and decision-record practices used across projects and regions.

  • Capability building: Grow architecture capability through hiring, training, communities of practice and design reviews.

  • Staffing: Work with delivery leadership to match architects to engagements.

Clients and market

  • Pre-sales: Shape solution architecture, estimates and proposals, especially where estate design carries the risk.

  • Client leadership: Build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders, from engineering leads to CTOs.

  • Thought leadership: Help shape service propositions and represent Datatonic as a technical authority at events and with Google Cloud.

Working with agents

You will use agents throughout engineering delivery and maintain the agents that support the architecture discipline, including their versioning, evaluation, operation and continuous improvement. This covers agents for option analysis, decision-record drafts, consistency checks against established patterns, and initial threat and cost assessments.

What you'll bring

  • Cloud architecture depth: Extensive hands-on experience designing and building production systems on Google Cloud (or AWS/Azure with a strong interest in GCP).

  • Engineering foundation: Proven depth in at least one engineering discipline (platform, data, software or ML engineering) at Senior 2 / L5 or above.

  • Demonstrated breadth: Evidence of systems design across disciplines, including networking, security, IAM, data platforms and application architecture.

  • Hands-on skills: Comfortable with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform), CI/CD, containers and Kubernetes, and at least one programming language such as Python.

  • Team leadership: Experience leading, mentoring or line managing engineers or architects, and raising the bar for a whole team.

  • Client leadership: Client-facing architecture leadership with senior stakeholders, including pre-sales and solution shaping.

  • Communication: Ability to explain complex trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, in writing and in person.

Bonus points if you have

  • Google Cloud certifications: Professional Cloud Architect or similar.

  • Complex estates: Experience with multi-cloud, hybrid or complex integration environments.

  • Architecture methods: Experience applying formal architecture methods (e.g. TOGAF) in complex delivery environments.

  • AI and data platforms: Experience architecting ML platforms, generative AI applications or agentic systems in production.

  • Consultancy background: Experience in a consultancy or professional services environment.

What's in it for you?

We believe in empowering our team to thrive, with benefits including:

  • 20 days of paid vacation per calendar year

  • Public Holidays for your Province of Residence

  • 5 Wellness days (sickness, personal time, mental health)

  • 5 Lifestyle days (religious events, volunteer day, sick day)

  • Matching Group Retirement Savings Plan after 3 months

  • Competitive Group Insurance plan on Day 1 - individual premium paid 100%!

  • Virtual Medicine and Family Assistance Program - 100% employer-paid!

  • Home office budget - We are 100% remote!

    • CAD $70/month for internet/phone expenses

    • Company-supplied MacBook Pro or Air

  • CAD $400/year for books, relevant app subscriptions or an e-reader.

  • Opportunities for paid certifications

  • Opportunities for professional and personal learning through Udemy Business

  • Regular company off-sites and meetups

Why Datatonic?

Datatonic is a UK-based company with an Americas division located in Canada. The Canadian team operates remotely, with members distributed across North and South America. This role is open to candidates located anywhere in Canada.

Join us to work alongside AI enthusiasts and data experts who are shaping tomorrow. At Datatonic, innovation isn’t just encouraged - it’s embedded in everything we do. If you’re ready to inspire change and deliver value at the forefront of data and AI, we’d love to hear from you!

Are you ready to make an impact?

Apply now and take your career to the next level.

#Amazonmexico


Key job responsibilities
- Create balance between “Work hard” and “Have fun” with associates under scope
- Ensure the team execution to accomplish the business goals
- Support process improvement activities associated with process inefficiencies and/or new functions currently not performed in day-to-day operations
- Processes Mapping activities.
- Assist in the development, documentation, deployment and monitoring the key business processes which support all internal processes of AMZL Mexico.

A day in the life
You’ll work shifts and be based at one of our operational sites. Your main focus will be to maintain safety standards within your team and across your site. You’ll also monitor and maintain process efficiency. Your days will always include prioritizing routine team management and daily operational tasks, alongside other tasks like individual escalations, process improvement work and wide-scale operational contingency planning.

Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles ‘last mile’ delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses. We utilize creative thinking and continuous improvement initiatives to get millions of physical products into the hands of our customers. Our goal is to make our customers’ delivery experience as smooth as possible and roll out global delivery solutions for our newest concepts, like Amazon Fresh, Prime Now and Amazon Restaurants.

There are two sides to what we do. Our ‘under the roof’ associates process millions of products for dispatch to our delivery teams. Our team is people-focused and supportive, particularly as lots of our people work through the night. We focus mostly on operations, with 24/7 shifts in most of our locations.

Meanwhile, our ‘on the road’ people work with Amazon Flex - a network of delivery contractors. Every year, we continually raise the bar for customer experience with new, innovative delivery services. We look for new ways to overcome industry wide logistics challenges and new ideas to reduce our carbon footprint, supported by a portfolio of new technology vehicles (including Electric Vehicles) and technology to help us do just that.

title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, INFRASTRUCTURE

As a Software Engineer on the Infrastructure team at SpaceXSI, you'll own the foundational cloud and networking layer that every service runs on: network foundations, container orchestration, edge and security infrastructure, and the compute runtimes that power production. SpaceXSI is one of the fastest-growing developer tools in the world, and you'll drive the cost management, regional deployment strategy, and infrastructure unification that make that growth possible. When your systems work well, every team is more productive, every product surface is more reliable, and Cursor can expand to serve developers everywhere.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own Kubernetes and cluster foundations: building and operating production clusters with proper service mesh, scaling, and ingress that teams can confidently deploy to

  • Design the geo-deployment architecture: building a replicable, robust process for deploying geo-replicated services across cloud regions and providers

  • Build edge and security infrastructure: designing the networking and security layer at the edge to protect against abuse, manage rate limiting, and optimize traffic routing

  • Own cost management and optimization: building attribution systems, identifying waste, and ensuring we're making smart tradeoffs between cost and reliability across all cloud spend

  • Unify the compute platform: defining a single, opinionated container orchestration strategy so every team gets consistent, reliable deployments out of the box

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Experience building and operating infrastructure on AWS, GCP, or similar cloud platforms.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Kubernetes experience at scale, including service mesh, autoscaling, and multi-region deployments

  • Experience building and operating production Kubernetes clusters at scale, including service mesh, autoscaling, and multi-region deployments

  • Understand edge networking, CDN/WAF architectures, and traffic management at the infrastructure level

  • Care about infrastructure-as-code, reproducibility, and making it easy for other teams to self-serve reliable infrastructure

  • Experience with cost optimization at scale or infrastructure migration/unification is a plus

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoying building the platform that makes every other team faster

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

Annual Salary:

$140,000 - $225,000 USD

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

title: Game Lead - Beach Bum
description:

Voodoo is a consumer tech company founded in Paris in 2013, with one mission: entertain the world. Today we are 1,000 people, generating $1b+ in annual revenue, profitably. We are looking for a Game Lead to take full ownership of our new game, from vision and product to team execution and business results.   • Proven track record of leading cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, hands-on environment.

title: Cloud Security Architect

Join our team and create your future.

As a senior member of our corporate security team, you will play a key role in designing and validating secure architectures across both cloud and hybrid environments. You’ll lead security architecture assessments, identify and mitigate potential threats, and help shape our overall security posture. This role involves close collaboration with stakeholders across the business and corporate IT and is primarily an internally facing position.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead security architecture assessments for new and existing applications, systems and integrations.
  • Partner with product engineering, DevOps, and compliance teams to develop secure architecture patterns that consider factors like data protection, access control, and segmentation.
  • Assess and validate security requirements based on the capabilities and risks of new and emerging information technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI).
  • Participate in threat modeling exercises to proactively identify security risks and guide secure design decisions.
  • Function as a subject matter expert across multiple security domains like cloud security posture management, identity and access management, and server/endpoint protection. Provide input into strategic security initiatives and roadmaps.
  • Stay up to date with emerging threats and trends. Assist with monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of information security safeguards and remediating discovered gaps.
  • Author code/scripts to audit, monitor, and/or remediate undesirable configurations within the environment.

title: Network Development Engineer, Network - Core
description:
MONA builds and operates the management plane, out-of-band (OOB) network, and automation systems that keep AWS's global network running. We run one of the largest fleets in Networking, growing from about 545K to 985K devices by the end of 2027, and we are redesigning the control layer underneath it. That means building the next generation of management networks for AWS, designed for Resilient Network Graphs (RNG), Machine Learning, and Intent-Driven Controls. We use software and AI, not manual process, to solve problems that people, runbooks, and tickets have solved until now.
As a Network Development Engineer II in Seattle, you'll work on several Senior Leadership initiatives at once. They include One Management Network, the next generation of how we build management connectivity across the fleet; faster on-site server builds; Initial Access, our new satellite-based product that supports multiple organizations in parallel and cuts the time to bring a new data center online; and support for new EC2 and security requirements. You'll join a team of network and software engineers working side by side, and you'll build and own pieces of this work from design through to launch. We want engineers who see a recurring network problem and build a product to solve it, not just a fix.


Key job responsibilities
Network Development Engineers in MONA build and operate the software and network systems that manage AWS's global network. You will design, deploy, scale, and sustain management plane, out-of-band, and automation platforms. You will use AI to troubleshoot and automate network operations, and you will write the documentation that lets others run what you build.
Design, build, and operate production automation and controller software that detects, diagnoses, and remediates network faults without manual intervention.
Use AI to automate repetitive operational work. Identify recurring network problems and turn them into reusable products, tools, and agentic workflows instead of one-off fixes, runbooks, or tickets.
Own projects from design through to operation in areas such as device management, out-of-band connectivity, Initial Access, network deployment and scaling, technology refresh, and sustaining engineering.
Make and implement changes on the network safely, using tooling, testing, and staged rollouts.
Work closely with software engineering and automation teams to define the tools and controllers that let us scale to a much larger fleet with a smaller team.
Use AI to troubleshoot network issues faster. Diagnose, mitigate, and resolve large-scale network events that affect significant AWS customers, using AI to triage, correlate alarms, and find root causes. Work with the highest-tier escalation engineers and resolvers, and drive root cause analysis and corrective actions through to completion.
Troubleshoot routing, interconnectivity, platform, performance, and configuration issues from Top of Rack to the network border. This includes low-level application behaviour, Unix systems, and modern network software tooling.
Partner with network engineering, hardware, and infrastructure teams on designs, configuration standards, and tooling. Make sure new designs and products roll out quickly and smoothly.
Maintain standards across the network toolset, and ensure our systems comply with those standards and policies.
Use operational data to find the largest sources of manual work and device downtime, and prioritise engineering effort against them, including out-of-service targets.
Deliver simple, sustainable, and repeatable solutions and processes. Convert standard operating procedures and runbooks into automated, AI-driven workflows, with guardrails, validation, and human review where the risk calls for it.
Take part in on-call, and reduce its load by cutting alarm noise and using AI and automation to handle common responses.
Write and review design documents, operational procedures, runbooks, and knowledge transfer material. Use AI to draft and update this material, and check it for accuracy before it is used.

A day in the life
Your day might start with a design review for a new controller, or a sync with the team on a workflow you're building. Mid-morning you could be debugging a stuck device in the out-of-band network, using AI to triage alarms and find the cause. Afternoons go to building: turning a recurring ticket into an automated workflow, testing it, and rolling it out in stages. You'll work with software engineers, hardware teams, and escalation resolvers, and write up what you learn so others can reuse it. Some days include on-call.

About the team
MONA sits inside AWS Network Fabric Engineering (NFE) and owns the management plane, out-of-band networks, and automation that keep AWS's global network running. You'll join a Seattle team that is part of a global group with hubs in San Jose, Sydney, and Dublin. Network and software engineers work side by side on the same problems, and you will learn from both. The fleet is growing from 545K to 985K devices by the end of 2027. Our work is moving from keeping that growth operable to redesigning the control layer beneath it, using software and AI to replace manual process.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, CORE SERVICES

As a Software Engineer on the Core Services team at SpaceXSI, you'll own the critical shared services that sit between our product surfaces and the infrastructure layer: auth, webhooks, and the backend systems that power agent workflows. SpaceXSI is redefining how developers write code, and your work is what makes that possible at scale. You'll build the systems that every product team depends on, ensuring they are reliable, well-abstracted, and ready for whatever comes next.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own authentication: designing and implementing a scalable auth architecture that secures one of the most widely-used developer tools in the world

  • Powering the agent backend: owning the infrastructure behind Cursor's agent workflows, optimizing for end-to-end performance and reliability as agents become central to the developer experience

  • Build a robust webhook server: handling high-throughput event delivery with proper retry semantics, dead-letter queues, and observability so external integrations just work

  • Harden SCM integrations: building resilient abstractions over source control providers so Cursor stays rock-solid regardless of third-party conditions

  • Drive end-to-end agent reliability: partnering with the client and inference teams to improve the full path from user action to agent response, closing the loop on one of the hardest problems in AI-powered development

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience building and operating backend services in production. Experience working with APIs and third-party integrations.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience with auth systems, API gateways, or webhook infrastructure

  • Experience working on agentic products or infrastructure and strong opinions on reliability and performance of complex multi-step systems

  • Care deeply about clean abstractions, well-defined service contracts, and making it easy for other engineers to build on top of your work

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoying owning the full lifecycle of production services

  • Experience with authentication/authorization frameworks (OAuth, JWTs, RBAC), event-driven architectures, or building developer-facing platform services is a plus

title: Technology Consultant, AI Security
description:
The Technology consultant will play a key role in delivering Plexal-led innovation and technology consulting programmes. Working as part of cross-functional consulting and research teams, the post holder will help organisations navigate the emerging technology landscape with a focus on AI Security, understand threat landscapes, assess opportunities and risks, and make informed strategic and operational decisions.

The role will involve contributing to research, analysis, stakeholder engagement and high-impact deliverables that support clients to de-risk potential investments, engage with the innovation ecosystem and identify deployable capabilities. The post holder will help map how AI Security and related emerging technologies are evolving, identify relevant capability in the UK and beyond, and translate technical, market and policy insights into accessible recommendations for clients.

We are a rapidly growing team and are actively looking to recruit exceptional individuals who want to work in an adaptive, fast-moving and collaborative environment. This role will be a fixed-term opportunity with the possibility of extension or to go permanent.
  • Shape insights about the future of AI Security and related emerging technology sectors.
  • Monitor AI Security technology trends, threat landscapes, policy developments, market needs and wider drivers to inform client advice and Plexal’s innovation work.
  • Assess AI Security and emerging technology propositions, including helping to interrogate vendor claims, understand technical trade-offs and identify risks and opportunities.
  • Engage with innovators, startups, vendors, clients and ecosystem partners to understand their needs, challenges, capabilities and growth requirements.
  • Support the design and delivery of end-to-end research and consulting projects for clients, including scoping research questions, applying qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, interpreting findings and turning analysis into clear recommendations.
  • Create high-impact deliverables, presentations and reports that help clients make decisions on cybersecurity, emerging technology strategy and innovation opportunities.
  • Proactively manage regular interaction, communication and collaboration with external stakeholders.
  • Support business development by contributing to public sector bids, bespoke proposals and the development of compelling client propositions.
  • Highly organised with a good understanding of innovation, collaboration and project management practices, tools and methodologies.
  • Analytical, with the ability to think critically and to understand, interpret and articulate complex technical, market and policy concepts.
  • Research and analysis skills, including strong analytical reasoning, methodological thinking, the ability to frame ambiguous problems and intellectual curiosity.
  • Ability to translate technical concepts, trade-offs, risks and opportunities for audiences ranging from senior leaders through to technical specialists.
  • A structured, concise communicator who can confidently use key tools including Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, as well as project management and brainstorming tools.
  • Competent at taking responsibility for producing high-quality deliverables and presentations for senior external audiences.
  • Experienced working within two or more of the following: a large innovation function, leading consultancy, technology startup or accelerator, research environment, AI Security organisation or technology delivery team.
  • Able to demonstrate strategic awareness across AI Security and emerging technology markets and provide an outside-in perspective to clients on emerging market needs, trends, opportunities and technologies.
  • Evidence of building trust-based relationships with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders, including innovators, startups, corporate clients, public sector clients or technical communities.
  • Able to communicate AI Security and emerging technology topics in an accessible and compelling narrative for non-specialist and specialist audiences.
  • Personally resilient, with the ability to stay focused on the overall objective, responding to challenges in a calm and measured way,
  • Energised by the challenges and opportunities presented by working for a high-growth company,
  • Passionate about the development of AI Security and other areas of emerging technology.
  • Flexible when working within a matrix structure with changing organisational and operational requirements.
  • This role may require some national travel for delivery of projects and travel to all Plexal sites.
  • Educated to a Bachelor-degree level or equivalent
  • SC or DV clearance desired
  • Due to the nature of this position, our work, and our client engagements, you must be willing and eligible to achieve a minimum of SC clearance. To qualify for SC clearance, you must be a British Citizen or have resided in the UK for the last 5 years with no extensive periods outside of the UK. Pre-existing SC welcome.For more information about clearance eligibility, please see https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/united-kingdom-security-vetting

Job Description:

Johnson & Johnson is currently recruiting for a Director of Sterility Assurance! This position will be performed fully onsite in Raritan, NJ.

Position Summary

The Director of Sterility Assurance, Cell Therapy Operations, provides site-level leadership and strategic direction for microbiological and virological control across cell therapy and lentiviral manufacturing at the Raritan facility. The role is accountable for establishing and sustaining an effective contamination control and sterility assurance program that protects product quality and patient safety, supports reliable operations, and maintains inspection readiness. The Director serves as the site’s primary subject matter expert and decision-maker for sterility assurance and contamination control and partners with Site and Global Quality, Manufacturing, Quality Control, Facilities and Engineering, MSAT, and Global Sterility Assurance/MQSA to align site practices with applicable health authority requirements, industry expectations, and scientific principles.


Major Duties
Site Sterility Assurance and Contamination Control Leadership


  • Own the Raritan sterility assurance and contamination control program, serving as the primary site point of contact, subject matter expert, and decision-maker for related matters.
  • Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve the site contamination control strategy, addressing viral, bacterial, fungal, mycoplasma, endotoxin, and other adventitious-agent risks.
  • Provide governance and oversight for microbiological and virological control programs, including environmental monitoring, incoming-material testing, in-process testing, lot-release testing, and stability testing.
  • Lead site risk assessments, gap assessments, mitigation plans, and sustainable remediation activities related to aseptic processing, biological contamination control, and sterility assurance.
  • Provide strategic input to facility and equipment design, process design, material and personnel flows, cleaning and disinfection, segregation controls, maintenance, environmental monitoring, and microbiological testing.
  • Lead the quality response to contamination events, sterility failures, microbiological excursions, and adverse trends; ensure scientifically sound investigations, root-cause analysis, and effective corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).
  • Review aseptic-processing and sterility-assurance performance indicators and trends; ensure timely, risk-based action plans and clear reporting to site and senior leadership.
  • Support regulatory inspections, internal audits, mock inspections, due-diligence activities, and other compliance initiatives as the site sterility assurance SME.
  • Monitor evolving regulatory requirements, industry expectations, and emerging technologies; translate relevant developments into timely, compliant, and practical site actions.
  • Coach and train employees to strengthen understanding of biological risks, contamination control, good aseptic practices, and expected behaviors.
  • Promote cross-site learning, capture lessons learned and near misses, and sponsor harmonization and continuous-improvement initiatives across the Advanced Therapies network.
  • Represent Raritan in network teams, governance forums, and appropriate external industry forums related to sterility assurance and contamination control, including implementation of applicable EU GMP Annex 1 requirements.

Leadership Team and People Management


  • Set functional priorities, objectives, and performance measures aligned with site and enterprise strategy, Our Credo, and applicable leadership principles.
  • Build and lead a high-performing, collaborative Sterility Assurance team through effective organization design, hiring, coaching, capability building, performance management, talent development, and succession planning.
  • Establish strong partnerships with Site Leadership, Manufacturing, Quality Control, Facilities and Engineering, MSAT, Supply Chain, Process Development, Analytical Development, Product Quality Management, and Global Quality organizations.
  • Coordinate quality activities across functions and sites to enable integrated, efficient, and compliant business processes.
  • Collaborate with Advanced Therapies Quality Leadership Team members to drive alignment, standardization, lifecycle management of GMP policies, and continuous improvement of the Quality Management System.
  • Represent Raritan in the planning, development, and execution of corporate Quality initiatives and provide input to resource and budget planning.

Qualifications

Education:


Bachelor’s degree in microbiology, pharmacy, engineering, chemistry or a related scientific / engineering discipline required; an advanced degree (MS/PHD) preferred

Required Years of Related Experience:

  • Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry, including Quality Assurance, Quality Systems, sterility assurance, contamination control, or microbiological quality oversight in a manufacturing environment.
  • Minimum of 6 years of people-management experience, with demonstrated success building, developing, and retaining high-performing teams.
  • Proven experience in quality leadership roles supporting commercial cGMP manufacturing operations.

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Expert knowledge of sterility assurance, contamination control, microbiology, and aseptic processing principles as applied to biological and cell therapy manufacturing.
  • Strong working knowledge of applicable cGMP regulations and guidance, including US FDA and European Union expectations and EU GMP Annex 1.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and implement risk-based sterility assurance strategies that support product quality, patient safety, operational reliability, and inspection readiness.
  • Experience leading responses to contamination events, microbiological excursions, sterility failures, and adverse trends, including investigations, root-cause analysis, and CAPA effectiveness.
  • Experience hosting or supporting global health authority inspections and presenting product, process, and quality-system information to regulatory reviewers.
  • Experience overseeing cGMP operations in a commercial manufacturing facility; experience with aseptic processing in ISO 5 environments and biosafety cabinets is strongly preferred.
  • Ability to influence across functions and organizational levels, communicate complex scientific and compliance topics clearly, and make balanced, risk-based decisions.
  • Strategic thinking, sound judgment, effective negotiation and conflict-resolution skills, and a strong continuous-improvement mindset.
