Job Description:

Principal Scientist, AI Co-Scientists - Synthetics Development


Why this role matters:

The future of small-molecule discovery and development depends on both translating scientific challenges into trustworthy AI-enabled capabilities and creating the data, information, and knowledge foundations on which those capabilities depend. This role will help Synthetics Development build and evaluate practical solutions spanning data science, machine learning, generative AI, information retrieval, document understanding, structured knowledge, and agentic workflows.


Position Summary

In this role, you will work at the interface of small-molecule science, data science, and artificial intelligence. In close partnership with chemists, analytical scientists, formulation scientists, process engineers, data scientists, and technology teams, you will investigate, prototype, and evaluate AI-enabled capabilities that address priority scientific challenges.

The role combines two closely connected responsibilities. You will de-risk new ideas through hands-on experimentation, focused technical spikes, and limited-scope proofs of concept. You will also design and implement the document-processing, metadata, retrieval, structured-data, ontology, and knowledge-graph components required to make scientific information usable by these solutions. In both areas, you will translate scientific needs into testable technical approaches and make feasibility, limitations, dependencies, risks, and potential value visible before broader investment.

Working as part of a cross-functional team, this role will contribute to scientific co-scientists, intelligent search, scientific data products, workflow automation, decision-support tools, and agentic workflows. The work will span practical experimentation and the implementation of reusable information foundations, including ingestion and document understanding, metadata and entity extraction, retrieval, controlled vocabularies, ontologies, and knowledge graphs. The role is not responsible for foundation-model development or production platform ownership. Its focus is hands-on development, technical learning, and creating robust components and evidence that help the team decide what to build and scale.

Why This Role Is Unique

This is a rare opportunity to help shape AI-native Synthetics Development by combining direct experimentation on real scientific challenges with the hands-on construction of the information and knowledge foundations required for credible scientific AI. You will work with scientists to understand their workflows, build and test targeted solutions, and ensure that the underlying scientific content can be processed, structured, retrieved, and reused effectively.

The resulting prototypes, ingestion and retrieval pipelines, structured knowledge assets, reusable components, experimental findings, and technical recommendations will inform capabilities across small-molecule discovery and development, including chemistry, formulation, process engineering, analytical sciences, and increasingly lab-integrated workflows.

Key Responsibilities

Applied AI Prototyping & Technical De-risking

• Design, implement, and evaluate limited-scope proofs of concept for priority scientific use cases.

• Run focused technical spikes to test assumptions, compare approaches, and assess emerging AI, machine-learning, and scientific-computing technologies.

• Translate scientific needs into testable hypotheses, representative experiments, success criteria, and clear technical questions.

• Rapidly build prototypes that make feasibility, limitations, dependencies, risks, and potential value visible before broader investment.

• Document experimental setup, results, trade-offs, and recommendations so that findings are reproducible and actionable.

• Identify when an approach should be refined, handed over for engineering and scale-up, or discontinued.

Scientific AI & Data Science

• Apply data science, machine learning, generative AI, information retrieval, and agentic approaches to scientific challenges in small-molecule discovery and development.

• Build experimental workflows that combine scientific data, documents, models, knowledge sources, APIs, and specialist tools.

• Investigate the behavior of AI-enabled workflows, including the quality of outputs, evidence use, tool interactions, failure modes, and sensitivity to input or configuration choices.

• Contribute reusable code, components, datasets, and experimental patterns that accelerate subsequent scientific AI work.

• Use quantitative and qualitative evidence to communicate what works, what does not, and what is required to progress a concept.

• Make scientific data AI-ready and science-ready by structuring, contextualizing, and curating experimental, analytical, process, molecular, and modeling data so it can be consumed by scientists, predictive models, co-scientists, and agents.

• Assess the AI-readiness of candidate data sources, identifying gaps in quality, completeness, context, and accessibility, and prioritize data improvements that are driven by concrete scientific use cases rather than completeness for its own sake.

Scientific Information, Retrieval & Knowledge Foundations

• Work with subject-matter experts to understand how scientists find, interpret, combine, and use information in their work.

• Design and test approaches for scientific search, retrieval, question answering, and information reuse.

• Contribute to document processing, metadata, structured representations, controlled vocabularies, ontologies, or knowledge graphs, applying FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable) principles pragmatically when these are needed to solve the scientific problem.

• Evaluate combinations of semantic search, keyword search, filtering, aggregation, structured queries, and knowledge-based methods.

• Help diagnose whether failures arise from data quality, missing knowledge, retrieval, reasoning, tool use, orchestration, or unclear requirements.

• Build reusable, well-documented data pipelines and data products, including ingestion, transformation, and contextualization, that connect data across laboratory, process, and scientific systems and make it accessible through APIs for AI, analytics, and automated workflows.

• Partner with data, architecture, and IT teams to leverage existing enterprise data platforms rather than recreating them locally, and provide the scientific perspective on semantics, provenance, and access.

Cross-Functional Delivery & Continuous Learning

• Act as a practical bridge between scientific SMEs and AI, data science, product, architecture, and engineering teams.

• Support co-design sessions, pilots, user testing, and technical demonstrations with scientific communities.

• Collaborate with engineering and platform teams to define the requirements and boundaries for solutions that are selected for further development.

• Contribute to evaluation, provenance, traceability, documentation, and governance appropriate to scientific and quality-conscious environments.

• Track relevant advances in AI, machine learning, scientific computing, retrieval, and agentic systems, and assess them through targeted experimentation rather than technology-led adoption.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a scientifically curious, pragmatic, and hands-on collaborator who enjoys turning ambiguous scientific challenges into concrete experiments. They can move quickly from a question to a working prototype, while maintaining enough rigor to distinguish a promising capability from a plausible-looking demonstration.

They combine strong data-science and software-development skills with scientific intuition, critical thinking, and clear communication. They are comfortable working between subject-matter experts and technical teams, challenging assumptions, learning from failed approaches, and balancing rapid exploration with reproducibility, maintainability, and responsible use.

Qualifications

Required

• Advanced degree in data science, computer science, bioinformatics, cheminformatics, computational science, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, engineering, or a related field; or equivalent relevant experience.

• 4+ years of relevant experience in applied data science, machine learning, scientific informatics, scientific software, pharmaceutical research and development, or a closely related environment.

• Hands-on proficiency in Python, including the ability to implement, test, debug, and maintain experimental AI and data-science workflows.

• Experience designing and executing technical experiments, prototypes, proofs of concept, or feasibility studies.

• Experience developing or evaluating AI-enabled scientific applications, co-scientists, decision-support tools, or tool-using agents.

• Experience with retrieval-augmented generation, semantic or hybrid search, vector databases, knowledge graphs, scientific NLP, or document intelligence.

• Experience working hands-on with scientific data, scientific documents, models, or scientific information systems, including data or document processing, metadata, retrieval, or structured knowledge.

• Familiarity with scientific data sources, predictive models, cheminformatics tools, simulation environments, experiment-design methods, or laboratory systems.

• Working knowledge of Git and reproducible software-development practices, with familiarity with Linux or shell environments, APIs, containers, and automated testing.

• Demonstrated ability to translate scientific needs into technical hypotheses, experiments, prototypes, and evidence-based recommendations.

• Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across scientific and technical disciplines and explain complex trade-offs clearly.

• A collaborative, iterative working style and the ability to manage ambiguity while maintaining scientific rigor, traceability, and focus.

Preferred

• Hands-on experience in small-molecule discovery or development, such as synthetic chemistry, analytical development, formulation, process development, high-throughput experimentation, or laboratory automation.

• Experience working in cross-functional, regulated, or quality-conscious environments where provenance, reproducibility, governance, and appropriate human oversight matter.

• Experience creating evaluation datasets, benchmarks, automated tests, or human-in-the-loop assessment processes for AI or data products.

• Experience integrating multiple scientific data modalities or combining documents, structured data, predictive models, simulations, and specialist scientific tools within a single workflow.

• Experience coaching colleagues, facilitating technical working sessions, or communicating emerging methods and experimental findings to scientific and technical audiences.

title: Software Engineer, Compute Infra
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, COMPUTE INFRA

As a Software Engineer on Compute Infra at SpaceXSI, you'll build the sandbox infrastructure that gives every agent its own VM. These VMs power coding agents, Grok Bot, reinforcement learning, and more. We operate one of the largest sets of sandbox clusters in the world, at millions of CPU cores, across third- and first-party datacenters. You'll own developing a cloud for agents, including the virtualization layer (Firecracker and Cloud Hypervisor microVMs), control plane scaling, and the networking/connectivity layer on top.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Rearchitect the control plane and scheduler to support 1 million concurrent VMs per cluster

  • Build a ublk block device that can dedupe, lazy load, and efficiently snapshot VM data

  • Design an egress proxy and network isolation to securely filter, monitor, and route agent traffic

  • Design resilient systems that can operate across a mixture of cloud and on-premise datacenters

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience building compute orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes, Mesos)

  • Experience building and operating large fleets of VMs or isolated sandboxes

  • Experience with the Linux kernel and virtualization technologies

  • Interest in the infrastructure primitives that future agents will require

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Onsite role: must be able to work in person at the San Francisco or New York office

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

Annual Salary:

$140,000 - $225,000 USD

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

title: Silicon Development Infrastructure Security, Annapurna ML
description:
We're looking for a Security Engineer to own the security posture of the cloud and hybrid infrastructure that powers silicon development at Annapurna Labs. You'll be a single-threaded security partner embedded in the ML Infrastructure team, working directly alongside software development engineers, system development engineers, and chip methodology engineers to keep the infrastructure that hundreds of chip designers depend on secure, compliant, and hardened against emerging threats.

This is a high-ownership role where you'll operate across the full security lifecycle: triaging and driving critical findings to resolution, building automated scanning and patching mechanisms, designing secure network architectures for vendor and partner onboarding, and turning repeated fixes into reusable automation and runbooks. You'll make security a seamless part of how the team builds and ships, not a gate that slows them down.

Key job responsibilities
• Vulnerability management — Own the security findings backlog end to end. Triage findings from security scanners and assessments (CVE/CVSS scoring, container and host scanning such as AWS Inspector), coordinate remediation with the engineering SMEs who own the affected systems, mitigate high-severity issues within agreed timelines, and drive measurable reduction of long-standing findings.
• Patching Automation — Keep server fleets (RHEL/Rocky Linux, Amazon Linux, and Windows Server, cloud and on-premises) current on critical security updates. Own and improve patching pipelines using dnf/yum, AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager, and golden-AMI pipelines, including emergency vendor patches on production systems. Establish a regular patching cadence and structurally eliminate recurring patch-drift findings.
• Vendor and partner onboarding — Run third-party security assessments for new technology partners and design isolated partner environments with least-privilege network and data access. Implement VPC segmentation, security groups and NACLs, Transit Gateway, AWS PrivateLink, client VPN, S3 bucket policies, and KMS encryption to enforce strict boundary controls.
• Identity and access — Design and audit access controls across multiple cloud accounts. Cover AWS IAM roles and policies, SCPs, IAM Identity Center, Active Directory and LDAP, Linux directory integration (SSSD, Winbind, PAM, Kerberos), sudoers, SSH key and certificate management, bastion hosts, and VPN. Fix privilege-escalation paths and unauthenticated endpoints (OIDC/SAML, Amazon Cognito, ALB authentication).
• Security automation — Build tools, dashboards, alerting, and AI-assisted agents that detect, explain, and fix security issues using Python, Bash, AWS Lambda, EventBridge, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub, and Amazon Bedrock. Turn repeated fixes into runbooks and reusable automation using infrastructure as code (AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform, Ansible).
• Threat modeling and design review — Review new infrastructure designs for security exposure using STRIDE and data-flow diagrams. Assess network ingress and egress, secrets handling (AWS Secrets Manager, KMS), TLS and certificate management, and logging coverage. Establish secure-by-default patterns that the broader team can adopt.
• Reporting — Produce clear weekly security status updates with metrics: finding counts by severity, SLA adherence, backlog trajectory, and workstream status.

A day in the life
Each day you will work with some of the best engineers in the industry to develop Machine Learning Accelerators. On-site in Austin, Texas, you will be part of the team that develops custom silicon and contribute to the security of the infrastructure that enables this innovation.
You might start your day triaging new vulnerability findings from overnight scans, assessing severity scores, and coordinating with the engineering SMEs who own the affected systems. You could spend your morning reviewing a vendor security assessment for a new technology partner, designing the isolated network environment they'll operate in, and ensuring least-privilege access controls are in place. In the afternoon, you might be building an automated remediation pipeline that patches critical CVEs across a fleet of Linux hosts, or refining a dashboard that gives leadership real-time visibility into the team's security posture and SLA adherence.

You'll participate in threat modeling sessions for new infrastructure designs, contribute to postmortems when security incidents occur, and continuously harden the systems that accelerate the path from RTL to silicon. Throughout the day, you'll balance immediate security needs, such as driving an emergency patch for a critical vulnerability on production systems, with longer-term investments like building AI-assisted agents that detect and explain security issues before they become findings. You'll write code, review infrastructure-as-code changes for security exposure, and collaborate across teams who depend on the secure foundations you build.

title: Solutions Architect, Software and Technology Companies (ISV)
description:
Are you passionate about cloud technology and helping customers innovate?

Join our AWS Solutions Architecture team in Sweden and empower Software, SaaS and Technology Companies to innovate at speed and scale with cloud technologies.

Solutions Architects work hand in hand with AWS customers to help them make the most of the Cloud. They are at the crossroads of business and technology and engage with organizations at all stages of cloud adoption. Solutions Architects are responsible for creating and presenting technical content and sharing best practices.

They work to understand the customer's business needs and give prescriptive guidance on how to create business value with technology. They help customer's validate their initiatives from ideation to proof of concept. Solutions Architects lead activities such as architecture reviews, white-boarding sessions, demos and technical workshops. They collaborate with other teams such as account management, professional services, Industry experts, support, service teams and the AWS partner ecosystem.

Amongst others you will be part of the design and building of reference architectures, proof of concepts and help customer deploy production workloads on AWS. You will also provide thought leadership and recommendations on cloud architecture, migration, modernization and operation. Build strong technical relationships acting as the voice of the customer internally to influence AWS service roadmaps.

At Amazon you will be encouraged and rewarded for doing what is right for the long-term success of the customer. We value your passion to discover, invent and build on behalf of customers.

Amazon has always been, and always will be, committed to diversity and inclusion. We seek builders from all backgrounds to join our teams, and we encourage our employees to bring their authentic, original, and best selves to work.

AWS Global Sales drives adoption of the AWS cloud worldwide, enabling customers of all sizes to innovate and expand in the cloud. Our team empowers every customer to grow by providing tailored service, unmatched technology, and dedicated support. We dive deep to understand each customer's unique challenges, then craft innovative solutions that accelerate their success. This customer-first approach is how we built the world's most adopted cloud. Join us and help us grow.

Key job responsibilities
- Work directly with strategic customers to accelerate their challenging, mission-critical projects and recommend best-practice architectures in line with their long-term business outcomes
- Build technical relationships with customers and operate as their trusted advisor. The best interests of the customer will shape the guidance you provide.
- Share the voice of the customer to inform the roadmap of AWS features.
- Participate in the creation and sharing of best practices, technical content and new reference architectures (e.g. white papers, code samples, blog posts).
- Evangelise and educate customers about AWS technology (e.g. through workshops, user groups, meetups, public speaking, online videos or conferences).
- Contribute to the growth of the Solutions Architecture organisation by interviewing candidates and having a voice in hiring decisions. You will also be helping others develop new skills by mentoring team members and identifying talent needs in the organisation.
- Develop areas of depth in technical domains relevant to our outcomes.

A day in the life
You will have the opportunity to work with account managers to help customers accelerate their cloud implementation to modernize their business on AWS. Working with these customers, you will help them transform existing workloads by designing modern target architectures optimized for business agility, innovation, performance, resiliency, cost, security, and more using both native and partner solutions.

Our teams focus on understanding customer key business drivers as well as the existing application architecture(s) to deliver a technical recommendation to the customer with a goal of designing a robust cloud architecture that can scale as their business requires.

About the team
Our Solutions Architecture team empowers innovators to invent on behalf of customers. We are obsessed with understanding each customer's unique objectives to deliver optimal architectures tailored to their needs. Our culture celebrates talented, curious, motivated team members who take ownership of projects. We move with urgency, take risks, learn continuously, and maintain a friendly, inclusive environment. Join our team if you are passionate about technology and delighting customers.

Your direct team is located across the Nordics and you would work in close collaboration with team members in Sweden and across borders.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

title: Engineering Manager, Agent & Product Security
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ENGINEERING MANAGER, AGENT & PRODUCT SECURITY

Cursor's agents work inside the codebases of some of the most security-conscious engineering organizations in the world, holding credentials, reading untrusted content, running tools, and shipping changes. Today they act on authority delegated per task. Where we're headed, they'll work more like coworkers: autonomous over long horizons, holding standing responsibilities, initiating work, and collaborating with people and other agents. The security models that the future needs, identity and accountability for autonomous workers, standing authority rather than per-task permission, agent-to-agent trust, oversight that scales with always-on autonomy, mostly don't exist yet.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Chart the path from supervised agents to trusted autonomous ones: define the security primitives that enable agent autonomy, and lead the team that builds them

  • Engineer the isolation that makes Cursor safe to run inside customers' most valuable codebases: tenancy, workspace, secret, and data protections designed for real adversaries

  • Build the authority infrastructure autonomous agents need: identity, scoped permissions, policy enforcement, and secure tool execution, so an agent can hold real responsibility with verifiable limits and full accountability

  • Build customer-facing security controls that are understandable, usable, and strong enough for Cursor's most security-sensitive customers, with crisp success metrics for security outcomes

  • Hire, coach, and grow a high-performing security engineering team while staying technically close to the work: write and review code where useful, and keep execution fast and technically grounded

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience leading engineering teams that ship production systems with high security, reliability, or platform stakes

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Wants a problem space where much of the answer isn't written down yet

  • Experience leading engineering teams shipping production systems with high security, reliability, or platform stakes, and you want a problem space where much of the answer isn't written down yet

  • Strong product and systems judgment: you can reason from user workflows to architecture, threat models, enforcement points, and operational tradeoffs, and you see security as something that enables product capability, rather than only restricting it

  • Understand modern application security, authorization, tenancy, identity, secrets, data isolation, and secure-by-default platform design

  • Good instincts about AI agents: how they use tools, where authority should come from, how prompt injection and exfiltration show up in practice, and how to build mitigations that hold up against creative adversaries

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity: you can set strategy where precedent is thin, commit to a direction, and stay close enough to the implementation to know when to change it

  • Able to partner well across product, infrastructure, ML, and customer-facing teams

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Onsite role based in New York or Palo Alto

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

$220,000 - $357,000 USD

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

title: JOB TEMPLATE - lead role
description:
About the Role

We're looking for a Head of Security to own security across Labhouse. Reporting to the CTO and as our first dedicated security hire, you'll assess our security end to end, tackle the biggest threats yourself, and sequence the program build by risk, starting with application security. You'll work closely with engineering, product and the founders, and build the team as we grow. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Application security. Build a secure development lifecycle with threat modeling and code review, and protect our mobile apps against reverse engineering, API abuse, account takeover and in-app purchase fraud.

  • Cloud and infrastructure. Harden our cloud and CI/CD with infrastructure as code, least-privilege access and secrets management.

  • Company security. SSO, MFA, device management, access reviews, and onboarding and offboarding for employees and vendors.

  • Vulnerabilities. Find and fix weaknesses in our code and in the tech we depend on, with pentests and a bug bounty or disclosure program.

  • Detection and response. Logging, monitoring, alerting, incident playbooks, post-mortems and, when needed, communication with users.

  • AI security. Guardrails against prompt injection and data leakage to AI vendors, and safe use of AI tools and agents internally.

  • Data protection and privacy. Encryption, data classification and retention, GDPR and app store privacy requirements.

  • Governance and compliance. Policies, risk assessments, vendor risk, and certifications like SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

About You

Experience:

  • You've led security at a fast-growing tech company as Head of Security, Security Lead or similar, ideally as the first or an early security hire.

  • Deep hands-on application security experience, including iOS and Android apps and their backend APIs. You know the OWASP MASVS and OWASP Top 10 well.

  • Strong cloud security skills on GCP: IAM, networking, secrets and infrastructure as code.

  • You read and review code, and write your own tools and automation, for example in Python or Go.

  • You've handled real security incidents from detection to post-mortem.

  • Pragmatic about risk: you focus on what matters most, know when to move fast and when to slow down, and make security easy for engineers rather than a blocker.

  • Self-driven, and comfortable taking ownership from day one.

  • You use AI tools daily and understand the risks they bring.

Problem-solving and ownership:

  • Excellent analytical skills and the ability to prioritize risks pragmatically in a fast-moving environment.

  • Self-driven, entrepreneurial attitude with the ability to work autonomously and take ownership from day one.

  • Strong judgment on when to move fast and when to slow down for security.

Communication:

  • Good level of spoken and written English.

  • Ability to explain security risks clearly to technical and non-technical colleagues and to collaborate with engineering, product, and IT.

Nice to Have:

  • Mobile reverse engineering and anti-tampering (Frida, Jadx, Ghidra, app hardening tools).

  • Fighting fraud in subscription apps: receipt validation, App Attest, Play Integrity and bot protection.

  • Securing LLM-powered features, AI agents and third-party AI APIs (OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, red-teaming).

  • Securing apps that handle sensitive user data, such as financial or document data.

  • Led a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification, or know GDPR, HIPAA, NIS2 and the AI Act well.

  • Certifications such as OSCP, OSWE, GMOB or CISSP. Useful, not required.

  • A track record in bug bounties, CVEs, open-source security tools or conference talks.

Application questions

  • Your first 90 days. You join as our first security hire. We ship several consumer subscription apps on iOS and Android, with a GCP backend and LLM-powered features. What do you look at first, and what are the top three risks you’d expect to find?

  • AI risk. How do you use AI tools in your own work? What’s one risk they introduce at a company like ours, and how would you mitigate it without banning them?

  • Which 2–3 sources do you rely on most to stay current on mobile, cloud or AI security, and what’s something useful you learned from one of them recently?

title: Research & Knowledge Analyst
description:
We invite you to review our current business services professionals openings to learn about the opportunities available across the firm.

About Us

Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP has forged a reputation as one of the most prestigious law firms in the world. Relying on innovation, intellect, teamwork and tenacity, our lawyers deliver the highest quality advice and novel solutions to our clients’ legal issues. We are known for handling the most complex transactions, litigation/controversy issues, and regulatory matters, as well as for the strong partnerships we build with clients and each other. Our attorneys, who reflect a broad range of experiences and perspectives, work together seamlessly across 50-plus practices and 21 offices in the world’s major financial centers.


The Opportunity

We are seeking a Research & Knowledge Analyst to join our Firm. This position will be based in our Los Angeles office (hybrid), with hours of Monday - Friday 11am-7m PT.

Responsible for researching and providing information, analysis and expertise to attorneys and business services professionals in all practice areas and offices of the Firm. Analyzes legal, corporate and general resources and communicates findings in a clear and concise manner.

Responsibilities

  • Supports complex research requests for Firm attorneys and business services professionals across the globe.
  • Performs cost efficient ready reference and in-depth research on legal, corporate and other topics using online and print resources to support all practice areas of the firm.
  • Uses question and answer skills to conduct effective reference interviews.
  • Distills research results into clear and concise reports of findings.
  • Provides full service research when working remotely or in the office.
  • Uses workflow software for the distribution and recording of requests.
  • Assists other department staff members when needed.
  • Demonstrates effective interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills to facilitate effective work relationships with others.
  • Manages Firm resources responsibly.
  • Complies with and understands Firm operation, policies and procedures.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Expertise in using computer-based research tools: Lexis, Westlaw, Bloomberg Law, Intelligize, Practical Law, Capital IQ, Deal Point Data, Pitchbook, VitalLaw, Docket Alarm, HeinOnline, and more
  • Broad and thorough knowledge of legal, business and financial information sources
  • Knowledge of relevant firm computer software programs (e.g., Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint), with the ability to learn new software and operating systems
  • Brings strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, close attention to detail, and sound, independent judgment and discretion.
  • Communicates clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing, with a courteous, professional, customer-focused approach, and works well independently and as part of a team.
  • Organizes and prioritizes work to meet deadlines across multiple projects with shifting priorities, works well under pressure in a demanding, fast-paced environment, and handles sensitive matters confidentially.
  • Ability to use discretion and exercise independent and sound judgment
  • Flexibility to adjust hours and work the hours necessary to meet operating and business needs

Education and Experience Required

  • Master’s Degree in Library Science or a minimum of two years directly related experience
  • Minimum of two years’ experience conducting research in a legal or corporate information center

Culture & Life at Skadden

What makes Skadden special is our people and the culture, community and spirit of collaboration we have created. We believe in teamwork and inspiring each other to be our best in an atmosphere that promotes professionalism and excellence in all that we do. We know that inclusion and drawing on the strength of a wide spectrum of talent only make us better and is vital to the firm's success. Our goal is for everyone at the firm to enjoy a challenging career with opportunities for development and growth and to support the well-being of our attorneys and business services professionals.


Benefits

The overall well-being of our team is important to us. We offer generous benefits to help you achieve wellness in all areas of your life.

• Competitive salaries and year-end discretionary bonuses.

• Comprehensive health care (medical, dental, vision), savings plan/401(k) and voluntary benefits.

title: Senior Staff Product Engineer
description:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

How we work

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 5, that looks like this:

What you'll be doing

  • Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

  • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

At Level 5 we'll also look for

  • Set technical direction on a hard problem other engineers built on, and been judged on whether you made them faster and safer rather than on the size of your team.

  • Held a quality bar across other people's work without becoming the gate they wait on.

  • Led cross-cutting or decoupling work that teams adopted because it was the best path, not because it was mandated.

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

  • B2B

    • 25 days of non-working + Polish bank holidays

    • £5,000 GBP budget for Learning & Development

    • Mental Health Support and Therapy via Spectrum Life

    • Optional for you: access to Private Healthcare via Luxmed + Multisport (fully funded by yourself as B2B Contractor)

    • Top-spec laptop (MacOS or Windows)

  • Contract of Employment (UoP)

    • £5,000 GBP budget for Learning & Development

    • 26 days of holiday + Polish bank holidays

    • Company pension

    • Company Sick Pay for 10 days at 100% salary

    • Mental Health Support and Therapy via Spectrum Life

    • Monthly Wellbeing allowance via Juno

    • Private Healthcare Insurance via Luxmed

    • Multisport - Classic level

    • Top-spec work equipment (MacOS, Windows + additional monitors, mechanical keyboards etc)

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Lead Hirer Interview

  3. Live AI Skills Assessment

  4. Values Interview with the CPTO

  5. Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

title: Community and Communications Associate
description:
This varied, hands-on role combines the day-to-day operation of our Reading innovation hub, with a particular focus on professional communications, community building through activities including hackathons, ideation sprints, maker workshops, group learning activities etc), and support for innovation projects and programmes. This role helps create and sustain an environment which encourages innovation so that it feels like a natural behaviour, rather than administering it.

You will work alongside our Community and Innovation Associate. Together, these two Associate roles share community, front-of-house and operational responsibilities, providing cover for one another. For this vacancy, we particularly seek communications and event-delivery experience, strong organisation skills and an interest in developing skills across innovation and programme delivery from conception to handover / execution.

This fast-paced, collaborative role suits someone with sound judgement and excellent people skills who is equally willing to undertake the practical tasks that keep a busy innovation hub running well. Communications and Content
  • Draft newsletters, social content and event communications using agreed templates and guidance on the key messages to convey. Develop new styles to keep the hub brand fresh and exciting.
  • Draft project updates, blogs, event write-ups, case studies and community stories for agreed channels, adapting material for different audiences with input from innovation and communications colleagues where needed.
  • Plan and maintain the communications and content calendar, plan their workload and source the information and materials needed to deliver agreed content by the required deadlines.
  • Use agreed platforms and templates, and online tools, to create and send emails and set up events, including using SharePoint, seeking advice or approval where required.
  • With guidance on the feedback required, create and use suitable feedback methods, such as forms, email and in-person conversations, then gather the results and provide trends and summaries to the wider team.
Events
  • Coordinate event logistics – e.g. creating registration pages, joining instructions, writing event copy, manage RSVPs, organise and set up the location including catering, liaise with speakers and other key stakeholders.
  • Support delivery on the day.
  • Monitor engagement and other agreed communications metrics, sharing results with the team to support future planning and improvements.
Community and Hub Operations
  • Share responsibility with the other Community and Innovation Associate for in-person hub cover, including an agreed early/late pattern.
  • Create a welcoming and inclusive hub experience for members, clients, visitors, partners and colleagues, building positive relationships and encouraging people to connect and take part.
  • Manage visitor bookings, access and practical arrangements for meetings and events.
  • Open, prepare and close the hub as required, ensuring it is ready for the working day and planned activities.
  • Maintain a presentable, organised and stocked environment, including room preparation, supplies and kitchen sundries.
  • Coordinate shared spaces, respond to routine requests and resolve straightforward operational issues, escalating facilities or IT problems where needed.
  • Share practical suggestions for improving the community and hub experience, based on feedback and day-to-day observations, for the wider team to consider.
  • Suggest methods / approaches that further nurture and grow the hub community, advancing reach and cultural impact.
  • Provide reasonable cover for the other Community and Innovation Associate during annual leave, absence and periods of increased activity.
  • Build relationships across clients, partners and delivery teams to connect people, share information and maintain momentum.
Programme and Project Support
  • Support project, programme and community activity by gathering updates, coordinating communications and keeping stakeholders informed from challenge triage and definition, through each project’s duration.
  • Maintain high-quality project documentation, communications and reporting materials.
  • Support regular project and programme reporting and meeting governance, including written status updates, stakeholder briefings, inputs, papers, actions and follow-up.
  • Proactively identify information gaps, blockers or emerging issues that could affect engagement or delivery, escalating where appropriate.
  • Strong written communication, with the ability to tailor messages, channels and timing to different audiences.
  • Excellent relationship-building and interpersonal skills; confident engaging diverse stakeholders and creating a welcoming community.
  • Highly organised and reliable, able to plan and prioritise multiple activities, deadlines and stakeholders.
  • Good judgement and attention to detail; able to take ownership and know when to seek advice or escalate.
  • Proactive and flexible, comfortable combining professional stakeholder work with practical hub administration.
  • Strong Word and PowerPoint skills, good working knowledge of Excel and ability to learn new digital tools quickly.
  • Develop metrics / objective key results to show and evidence effectiveness of actions against pre-agreed goals / objectives.
  • Practical experience planning and delivering events, workshops, meetings or community engagements.
  • Experience creating professional communications for different audiences.
  • Experience gained in events, communications, marketing, community engagement, hospitality or a comparable environment.
  • Experience developing communications or engagement plans and content across newsletters, digital platforms, social media, case studies or similar channels.
  • Experience supporting projects or programmes through trackers, actions, risks, reporting or governance.
  • Experience working at pace with multiple stakeholder groups, ideally in innovation, technology, defence, government or another complex environment.
  • Energised by working in a fast-paced, high-growth organisation and innovation environment.
  • Confident engaging with diverse stakeholder groups.
  • A natural community-builder who enjoys connecting people, creating energy and helping others feel welcome and able to contribute.
  • A motivated self-starter who takes initiative, exercises good judgement and is comfortable operating with ambiguity.
  • A collaborative team player who is equally willing to lead an activity or undertake routine tasks that support colleagues and the hub.
  • Curious, adaptable and interested in developing broader innovation and programme delivery capability.
  • This is a predominantly site-based role because the team provides in-person operational cover for the Reading innovation hub.
  • The Associate team covers the hub’s approximately 08:00–17:30 operating day through an agreed early/late rota. Individuals are not routinely expected to work the full period
  • Flexibility is required to cover colleague annual leave and absence and occasionally support activities outside normal hours. Additional hours are managed through Plexal’s TOIL arrangements.
  • The majority of the working week will be based at the Reading hub. Some home working may be possible where operational requirements and Associate cover allow.
  • May require business travel across Plexal sites.
  • Ability to manage and influence through face-to-face and virtual team environments.
  • Must be able to achieve a minimum of SC clearance.
  • This job profile is not exhaustive; the post holder may undertake other reasonable duties as directed by the Line Manager.

As a start-up, we thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced work environment dedicated to empowering innovators. We embrace individuals who leverage technology and creativity to tackle our greatest challenges head-on. We strongly advocate for maintaining a harmonious work-life balance, our goal is to ensure every member of our team can authentically be themselves and live their best lives. We firmly believe that innovation and creativity flourish when we cultivate a diverse workforce, comprising highly skilled individuals with a wide range of perspectives to contribute.

In return we will offer you:

  • Salary: Circa £35,000 depending on skills and experience
  • Annual bonus scheme
  • A generous pension scheme (with a company contribution of up to 10%)
  • Private healthcare, life assurance and critical illness cover
  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays

title: Program Manager II - Devices Beta, Amazon Devices Beta
description:
The Amazon Devices Beta (ADB) Team is your hall pass to play at work!! We are responsible for the “real world validation” for Kindle eReaders, Fire Tablets, FireTV products, and Emerging products…think, Amazon Smart Oven and Amazon Basics Microwave. How do we do this? By playing with these products every day! We work with product and engineering teams to prepare new product launches, system software and app updates, and marketplace expansions. Our goal is to gather feedback and expose issues and bugs prior to the product launching, so we delight our customers with products beyond their expectations.

Key job responsibilities
The ADB Team needs an experienced Program Manager to help us build and execute programs to validate the customer experience during the product development cycle. You will work with end users and a wide variety of internal teams to develop the strategy and execute the program to confirm from a customer perspective we are ready to launch. You will be a “hands on” contributor to support and troubleshoot issues, resolve problems, and keep the feedback flowing. Along the way, you’ll identify opportunities for improvements and put processes and tools in place to help us scale. You will track, communicate status, and independently drive issues to resolution. Cross-team coordination, program management, and an ability to learn and understand new technologies are essential.

A day in the life
Our programs are global and composed of Amazon employees across the company. We put pre-released devices and/or software in the hands of beta testers who represent our target customer profile ("people all about smart home automation", "people who love to read", or "people who are native speakers of French"). Working with our product team counterparts, we ask testers for “no holds barred” feedback to tell us what works and what needs to be fixed. Our bar is always being raised and we strive to achieve an Amazon 4-Star or better product every time!

About the team
The Amazon Devices Beta Team is responsible pre-launch customer feedback for our products. The team is composed of program managers who love technology and devices. Together with product owners, we plan and execute beta programs focused on gathering early customer feedback to help Amazon ship devices and software that delight customers. Our objective is to leverage the voice of the customer to validate and improve the experience and make an informed decision regarding launch readiness.

title: Data Center Technician, DCC Communities
description:
Join our dynamic AWS team and become a critical guardian of global cloud infrastructure! You'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of the world's most innovative technology platform, ensuring seamless data center operations that power millions of businesses and services worldwide.
Data Center Technician position involves in-depth hardware and network diagnostics followed by physical repair as well as participating in an on-call rotation.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Performing server rack installations, hardware break-fix on various components, troubleshooting network issues, and responding to operational incidents that impact service availability, escalating to senior technicians and management as needed/required
- Serving as a primary contact point for both internal and external stakeholders, including engineers, software developers, vendors, and contractors
- Performing on-call duties and participating in scheduled maintenance and change management activities
- Contributing to documentation and process improvement initiatives based on your analysis of operational issues
- Helping to train and onboard new team members
Physical requirements:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 40 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 41+ pounds
- Working in cramped and/or elevated locations
- Bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching
- Standing and walking for up to 8+ hours a day
- Ascending and descending ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation
- Work in a noisy environment
- Work shifts longer than 8 hours to support 24/7 operations (covering both night and day shifts).
- This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.
Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility
- Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
As a Data Center Technician professional, you have industry-leading technical abilities and demonstrate a breadth of knowledge while you:
- Take ownership of technical issues brought by their customer base, engaging other teams when needed to drive resolution
- Solve problems at their root and step back to understand the broader context
- Maintain service level agreements through the implementation of proactive issue detection and reporting
- Are biased to act in the absence of direction or support
- Improve effectiveness through process innovation

You will be required to work shift work that will include days/nights/weekends/holidays. Traveling within and outside of regional work area is required. You will be responsible for having a reliable personal vehicle and valid driver's license to travel within the regional work area, as company transportation will not be provided.

title: Junior Software Developer - Python & Web Applications (m/f/d)
description:
At Statista, we’re all about facts and data, for we are the world's leading business data platform. By providing reliable and easy-to-use data as well as various data analytics products and services, we empower people worldwide to make fact-based decisions.

Founded in Hamburg in 2007, we have quickly grown into a global company with offices in major cities such as London, New York, Berlin and Tokyo. And we still have a lot of plans. Our constant growth does not only prove our success, but also keeps creating new development and career opportunities for our employees.

We value and celebrate our diverse culture. You are welcome here for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or whether you prefer bar graphs to pie charts. Your story matters – keep writing it as part of our team.

Are you ready to join us?

Your team
This job is with Statista R, a vertical business unit of Statista.

Statista R is a world leader in the creation of company, brand, and product rankings and top lists, based on comprehensive market research and data analysis: Statista R recognizes the best.

With a team of over 100 expert analysts and in cooperation with more than 40 high profile media brands across all continents like Forbes, TIME Magazine and Newsweek, Statista R creates transparency for consumers and business decision makers and helps companies build trust and recognition across a plethora of industries and product categories. A team of over 50 licensing specialists based in New York, Hamburg, Tokyo, and Singapore offers the awarded companies meaningful and eye-catching opportunities to communicate their success via logos and other award related products. Visit for further information about Statista R and our rankings.

Your Role

  • Design, build and maintain web applications for working with data as a core part of your role, mainly using Python frameworks such as Django and Streamlit

  • Work closely with our senior Data Engineer and other experienced data professionals who build our analytics products and pipelines, learn hands-on about our AWS cloud environment and ETL processes, and help build reliable data pipelines and PostgreSQL queries

  • Prepare, transform and validate data so our applications and analyses rest on a solid foundation

  • Create visualizations and insight reports that make findings clear and actionable, both to make our analyst team's processes more efficient and to produce strong client-facing materials

  • Work with teammates to turn analytical questions into usable features and workflows, and develop repeatable ways to build expertise and value for our stakeholders

  • Support projects based on large-scale, survey-based market research data, and help develop methods that complement our existing ranking products

Your Profile

  • Solid hands-on skills in Python, gained through professional work, internships, research, or your own projects. Experience coding in R is advantageous

  • Experience building web applications with Django and/or Streamlit is a strong plus. Knowledge of PostgreSQL or another SQL database, and basic HTML, CSS or JavaScript, is also a plus

  • A basic understanding of cloud environments such as AWS and of ETL concepts, and the motivation to grow these skills alongside experienced colleagues

  • Hands-on experience working with data, including querying, cleaning, analyzing, visualizing and checking data quality

  • Clean coding habits that make teamwork easy, such as readable code and basic Git workflows

  • Enjoyment in building tools other people use, a collaborative way of working, and the curiosity to dig into unfamiliar problems

What we offer

In addition to our great team, culture, and our shared goal of empowering people with data, there are many other things that make Statista a great place to work! Join us and benefit from:

  • Work from abroad up to 30 calendar days a year

  • Hybrid work and flex-time

  • International team and social events

  • Subsidized urban mobility and access to fitness and wellness options

  • Free access to Langdock and all its amazing functionalities

  • Career & training opportunities

  • Attractive locations and modern offices

  • Mental health support with OpenUp

Some of the benefits listed here apply only to the German entity and to Junior-level roles or above.

title: Bathing Technician - VIP Petcare
description:
Overall Job Summary

As a Bathing Technician you will play a positive role in the lives of pets and pet parents by providing a bathing experience that includes compassion, gentleness, reassurance, safety and comfort in a non-scissor environment. You will be key in delivering our brand promise to pet parents, partners and other team members by living the values and promoting a culture of safety in the grooming environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (Min 5%)

  • Safely restrain / hold pets for wellness procedures including nail trims/grinding, anal gland expression and clipping
  • Make recommendations for services and products for every pet, every time, based on the pet’s lifestyle and an understanding of canine hygiene and environment.
  • Scan pets for microchips
  • Maintain a clean and sanitary work environment by disinfecting surfaces and equipment in between each pet
  • Promote a culture of safety in your salon and live our values, while continuing to reinforce our brand promise with pet parents, partners, and team members

  • Collect payment, dispense, and label medication, and review discharge paperwork with pet parents.

  • Assess dog’s coat conditions and partner with groomer on service recommendations

  • Supervisor if supplies are needed or if equipment is damaged or needs repaired.

  • Experience with pet salon equipment handling and maintenance
  • Familiar with safety and sanitization protocols
  • Understanding of canine behaviors

Physical Requirements

  • Walking

title: Regional Director, Strategic Enterprise
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. title: Senior Hardware Reliability Test Engineer – Electrical Systems & Power Electronics
description:
Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services.

This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation.

Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference.

Role Summary

This position develops the test capabilities and experimental evidence needed to assess the reliability of electrical hardware. You will evaluate PCB assemblies, power supplies, AC/DC and DC/DC converters, voltage regulators, and power distribution assemblies through controlled electrical and environmental testing.

A central part of the role is creating practical test solutions: designing and building custom jigs and fixtures, integrating instruments and electronic loads, writing automation, and tracking performance throughout accelerated stress testing. You will work directly with the Systems team to establish realistic operating conditions and evaluate how components, boards, and power modules behave within the complete system.

Electrical failure analysis is also part of the work. You will investigate abnormal behavior, reproduce failures, isolate suspect components or circuits, and collaborate with the Failure Analysis and Design teams to connect test results with failure mechanisms and verify corrective actions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, assemble, and troubleshoot custom electrical test jigs, fixtures, interface boards, load circuits, and wiring harnesses for power electronics and system reliability testing.

  • Work directly with the Systems team to establish representative workloads, power sequencing, electrical interfaces, operating limits, and monitoring requirements.

  • Translate product requirements and reliability risks into test plans with defined stress conditions, sample sizes, durations, measurements, and acceptance criteria.

  • Build automated test setups integrating programmable power supplies, electronic loads, switching hardware, sensors, and data acquisition equipment.

  • Develop Python or equivalent software for instrument control, test sequencing, continuous monitoring, fault capture, and analysis.

  • Execute accelerated life testing, burn-in, powered temperature cycling, power/load cycling, and biased temperature/humidity testing based on the hardware and failure mechanisms being evaluated.

  • Establish electrical baselines and monitor changes before, during, and after stress. Measurements may include efficiency, regulation, ripple and noise, transient response, startup/shutdown behavior, protection functions, and thermal derating.

  • Investigate electrical failures using schematics, PCB layouts, component datasheets, and bench measurements to isolate shorts, opens, leakage, intermittent behavior, and performance degradation.

  • Reproduce system-level anomalies in controlled experiments with the Systems team and correlate electrical results with physical failure-analysis findings.

  • Use DOE, statistical reliability analysis, and physics-of-failure methods to assess degradation, compare design alternatives, and evaluate component or process changes.

  • Partner with Design, Failure Analysis, Mechanical/Thermal Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, and suppliers to validate corrective actions and communicate reliability risks.

  • Maintain calibrated, repeatable test setups with appropriate electrical protection and interlocks.

  • Document fixture designs, test procedures, results, and investigation findings so that methods can be reproduced and conclusions can guide engineering decisions.

Skills and Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in electrical testing, hardware validation, reliability engineering, or electrical failure analysis.

  • Demonstrated ability to turn electrical test requirements into working laboratory setups, including custom fixtures, interface circuitry, wiring, and instrumentation.

  • Strong knowledge of PCBAs, power conversion, voltage regulation, power distribution, and electronic circuit behavior.

  • Practical experience with oscilloscopes, differential and current probes, programmable power supplies, electronic loads, multimeters, power analyzers, source measurement units, and data acquisition systems.

  • Proficiency in Python, LabVIEW, or equivalent tools for test automation and data analysis.

  • Strong circuit-debugging skills and the ability to interpret schematics, PCB layouts, and component specifications.

  • Understanding of accelerated testing, electronics failure mechanisms, reliability statistics, and measurement uncertainty.

  • Familiarity with relevant JEDEC and IPC test methods and qualification practices.

  • Ability to collaborate directly with Systems engineers, communicate technical findings clearly, and manage multiple laboratory investigations.

  • BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Desired Skills and Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

  • Experience integrating electrical test fixtures with environmental chambers and automated monitoring systems.

  • Hands-on work with high-current power modules, converters, and power delivery assemblies.

  • Experience with board bring-up, system integration, embedded firmware, Linux-based test environments, and hardware communication interfaces.

  • Knowledge of reliability concerns associated with power semiconductors, capacitors, magnetic components, connectors, and solder joints.

  • Ability to interpret microscopy, thermal imaging, X-ray, and cross-sectional findings in the context of electrical failures.

Location: Sunnyvale, CA

The base salary range for this position is $190,000 to $230,000 annually. Actual compensation may include bonus and equity, and will be determined based on factors such as experience, skills, and qualifications.

Why Join Cerebras

People who are serious about software make their own hardware. At Cerebras, we have built a breakthrough architecture that is unlocking new opportunities for the AI industry. With dozens of model releases and rapid growth, we’ve reached an inflection point in our business. Members of our team tell us there are five main reasons they joined Cerebras:

  1. Build a breakthrough AI platform beyond the constraints of the GPU.

  2. Publish and open source their cutting-edge AI research.

  3. Work on one of the fastest AI supercomputers in the world.

  4. Enjoy job stability with startup vitality.

  5. Our simple, non-corporate work culture that respects individual beliefs.

Find out more about what it's like to work at Cerebras here!

Apply today and become part of the forefront of groundbreaking advancements in AI!

Cerebras Systems is committed to creating an equal and diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We believe inclusive teams build better products and companies. We try every day to build a work environment that empowers people to do their best work through continuous learning, growth and support of those around them.

description:

title: Quality Assurance Engineer
description:

As a Quality Assurance Engineer at C.A. Murren and Sons, you will be considered an important part of the team as you bring your expertise in meeting organizational objectives.
