title: Senior Product Engineer
description:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

How we work

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 3, that looks like this:

What you'll be doing

  • Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

  • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via .

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Lead Hirer Interview

  3. Live AI Skills Assessment

  4. Values Interview with the CPTO

  5. Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

  • Educate HCPs on reimbursement processes, claims submissions, procedures, and coding requirements of payer organizations (local payers, government payers, etc.) for core and launch products.

Serve as subject matter expert regarding education and insights on access and affordability solutions across multiple payer types and plans (i.e., Medicare, Medicaid Managed Care, Commercial).

Market Access Expertise:

  • Remains current on and anticipates changes in product coverage and access knowledge, marketplace conditions, and stakeholder practices to deliver the most effective delivery of approved materials

QUALIFICATIONS:

REQUIRED

  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience
  • Account Management and/or Reimbursement experience working in the provider office setting, building strong customer relationship

title: Solutions Architect, Central Europe

Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Expand SpaceXSI Across the Organization: Identify where SpaceXSI should expand next inside the customer environment; help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption; design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups; partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale; work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments

  • Help Make SpaceXSI Indispensable: Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness; monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on SpaceXSI over time; support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction; help customers build workflows they can't imagine operating without

title: Agentic AI Engineering Co-op – Active Noise Cancellation | Fall 2027
description:

Job Description

ABOUT BOSE CORPORATION

At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

ABOUT THE CO-OP PROGRAM


Bose Corporation is seeking students to participate in our Co-op Program who share our belief that sound is power. During the six-month co-op, students will have the chance to apply classroom learning in a hands-on work environment. Co-op participants will network across the business to gain diverse perspectives within Bose Corporation. Additionally, co-ops will connect with other students and colleagues, building valuable professional relationships for the future.


Fall Co-op: Candidates must be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) in a hybrid, in-office format from July 12 through December 17, 2027. No relocation assistance is available.


Being currently authorized to work in the U.S. is a precondition of employment for this position.


THE ROLE

We're looking for a Co-op to join our research team and explore how AI agents can support engineers working on active sound management technologies.

The role sits at the boundary between signal processing and software engineering. You don't need to be an active noise control expert on day one; you will learn the domain from senior engineers who build these tools. You should be a strong programmer who is comfortable reading engineering code and asking why it works.

In this role, you will:

  • Capture expert knowledge. Work with senior engineers to document engineering workflows: key decisions, heuristics, failure modes, and what a finished result looks like.
  • Modernize engineering tools. Refactor existing tools into modular functions with well-defined inputs and outputs.
  • Connect tools to AI agents. Make engineering functions available to LLM-based agents using Python and modern tool-calling interfaces.
  • Measure what works. Build an evaluation framework that compares agent results against expert-produced references.
  • Build in safeguards. Implement automated checks that keep agent outputs within engineering and safety limits.
  • Prototype and demonstrate. Build an agent-assisted workflow and demonstrate it on a real engineering use case.
  • Report and document. Present your results and document your work so the team can build on it after your term.

  • To excel in this role, candidates should possess the following:
  • Currently pursuing a PhD or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
  • Strong Python: writing modular code, packaging functions, using git, and writing tests
  • Working knowledge of MATLAB, enough to read and refactor existing engineering scripts
  • Signal processing fundamentals: FFT, spectra, transfer functions, coherence, and digital filters
  • Hands-on experience calling an LLM API or building a simple agent or tool-using app, in a project, course, or internship
  • Clear written communication; the role involves documenting expert knowledge, not just code

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Coursework or projects in adaptive filtering, active noise control, or acoustics
  • Background in optimal filtering, multichannel systems, or control systems
  • Familiarity with Simulink
  • Experience with LLM agent frameworks, tool calling, or agent protocols such as MCP
  • Experience designing evaluations or test suites for ML or LLM systems
  • Experience integrating MATLAB and Python
  • Comfort with large measurement datasets (time series, .mat or HDF5 files) and with plotting results clearly

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • How active noise cancellation systems are measured, designed, and optimized
  • How to turn expert engineering judgment into reliable, testable software
  • How to build and evaluate an LLM agent for a real engineering task where reliability matters

At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! title: Head of Growth Engineering
description:
About Plaud Inc.

Plaud is building the real-world AI interface for professionals to amplify intelligence, elevate productivity and performance, loved by over 3,000,000 users worldwide since 2023. With a mission to amplify human intelligence, Plaud captures, structures, and compounds the intelligence generated in conversations — so humans can think better, decide faster, and execute with clarity.

Plaud Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated, San Francisco-based company. With GDPR, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and EN 18031 compliance, Plaud is committed to the highest standards of data security and privacy protection.

To learn more about Plaud, please visit and follow along on Instagram, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube.

Why You Should Join Us

Plaud is building the next generation intelligence infrastructure and interfaces to capture, extract, and utilize intelligence from what people say, hear, see, and think.

  • Plaud is a bootstrapped, skyrocketing, profitable company with a $300M revenue run rate achieved in just three years.

  • Define the next-gen paradigm for human-AI interaction.

  • Gain exposure to cutting-edge AI for Pro tools and play a direct role in our global expansion.

  • Work with passionate teammates who value innovation, collaboration, and customer success.

  • Grow your career in a culture that champions continuous learning and fast career development.

  • Market-competitive compensation, global exposure, and a vibrant, creativity-fueled work atmosphere.

Growth is a brand-new team at Plaud, and you would build it from the start. You'd own onboarding, experimentation and funnel optimization across every surface our users touch: the device, mobile, web and desktop. You start with 3M+ users and a device already in their hands. We want someone who has run growth engineering at a product-led company, lives in experiments and still ships code.

What you will do

  • Build Plaud's Growth engineering team from scratch, and define its strategy for onboarding, experimentation and funnel optimization across every surface users touch: the device, mobile, web and desktop.

  • Hire, lead and grow the team (full-stack, mobile and data-minded engineers), and stay hands-on in the code when it helps.

  • Own the end-user onboarding experience, from device setup and signup through first run and activation, so new users get value in their first session.

  • Build and run a high-tempo experiment program on our experimentation platform, with sound statistics, clear readouts and shared learnings.

  • Find and fix the biggest drop-offs in the user funnel, and turn what works into reusable patterns other product teams can adopt.

  • Partner with the Data team on funnel instrumentation and experiment data the whole company can trust.

  • Work closely with the product, pricing and app framework teams so that experiments ship safely behind feature flags on every surface.

  • Report on activation, conversion through the funnel and experiment velocity, plus the guardrail metrics that must not get worse.

Skills, qualifications and experience we look for

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years leading growth engineering at a product-led consumer or prosumer company.

  • Proven track record shipping onboarding and activation improvements that moved measurable metrics.

  • Deep experimentation expertise: test design, statistical power, guardrail metrics, and knowing when not to run a test.

  • Experience optimizing funnels across several surfaces (mobile, web, desktop). Hardware or device onboarding is a strong plus.

  • Strong full-stack skills (React, mobile, and a backend language such as Go, Python or Node.js) and comfort writing production code.

  • Experience with experimentation and analytics tools such as PostHog, Amplitude or Segment.

  • Has built a team from scratch, with excellent collaboration across Product, Design and Data.

What we offer

  1. Meaningful Ownership An Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) that gives a real stake in Plaud’s long-term success.

  2. High-Impact Environment Work in a fast-moving, product-driven environment where your ideas directly shape the future of AI productivity.

  3. Cutting-Edge AI Tools for Productivity Access to best-in-class AI tools, including Gemini, Claude Code, and other frontier AI systems to maximize engineering and execution efficiency.

  4. Best-in-Class Equipment Choice of top-spec laptops, high-performance workstation setups, and cutting-edge Plaud devices for all new hires.

  5. Team & Culture Annual company offsites, team events, and a culture that values craftsmanship, ownership, and velocity.

Disclaimer: Plaud is and will continue to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

title: Sr. Design Technologist, Advertising UX Design Systems
description:
At Amazon we put our customers first in everything we do – including our advertising programs. We’re building solutions that enable brands to connect with their customers, globally and at scale, where they shop, read, watch videos, and share online. The Advertiser User Experience (AUX) team excels at distilling the needs of a diverse user base into experiences that balance efficiency with robust utility. We’re looking for a new teammate who is enthusiastic, empathetic, curious, motivated, reliable, and able to work effectively with a diverse team of peers; someone who will help us amplify the positive & inclusive team culture we’ve been building.

The Storm Design System team within AUX defines the UX foundations, guidelines and owns the design system that enables teams across Amazon Advertising to design on-brand advertiser experiences efficiently and at scale. We’re looking for a Sr. Design Technologist (DT) to define and deliver tooling solutions for our design system to support designers and developers worldwide. This individual will help build AI-based ecosystems to rapidly accelerate builders’ access to high-quality prototypes, user-centered writing guidelines and research agents to pair product design with customer feedback. This person will create and maintain new web/native-based applications, create services, and launch plugins for design applications (e.g., Figma). These solutions will require connections to 1P and 3P APIs/endpoints, documentation and presentation to help streamline workflow and transitions between designer and developer teams. Key goals of this role include: 1) unlock critical UX resources, democratizing and making them accessible for utilization in all stages of the product development lifecycle; and 2) automate inefficiencies across teams by staying close to customer needs.

You'll have space to experiment with emerging technologies and workflows, with the expectation that experiments lead to shipped solutions that measurably improve how teams work.

As a Sr. DT in AUX, you will be part of a cross-functional team of designers, technologists, researchers, front-end engineers and program managers. You will be responsible for creating solutions that drive scale across design teams using the Storm design system.

Key job responsibilities
Actively participate in concept development and design ideation as part of a cross-functional team.
Rapidly build and iterate on functional prototypes that express design intent, using the best and most appropriate tools and techniques for the task.
Bring strong UX intuition — interpret design intent, identify usability issues, and ensure design quality carries through from concept to working code.
Partner with engineering to ensure that interactive techniques and technologies translate through to scalable tools and services.
Partner with design and research to create realistic prototypes to test with end customers
Be able to work creatively through and around perceived limitations and/or challenges imposed by the delivery platform to create delightful experiences for customers.
Lead large, wide impact DT projects. Examples could include a specific tool or service that supports many disparate areas of the site or product line.
Lead others and set direction in the face of ambiguity
Evaluate and document any new creative and/or engineering standards or patterns that could arise from your work
Effectively present work to all levels of leadership

About the team
The Advertiser UX (AUX) team serves as the strategic design center for Amazon Ads, designing end-to-end experiences for advertisers, publishers, partners, and internal account teams across the Ads Console, PubTech, and Sales organizations. Our vision is to enable advertisers of all sizes to effortlessly harness advertising potential through intuitive, intelligent, and unified experiences. Operating across multiple product teams, AUX carries a view of our advertisers that no single domain holds, enabling us to look around corners, inform the creation of bar-raising experiences, and connect the quality of those experiences to the real value they deliver.

title: Principal Technical Program Manager, AWS Bedrock AgentCore
description:

In this role, you will operate with complete independence across VP organizations, defining program strategy, driving clarity where none exists, and making trade-offs between business opportunities, resources, and long-term sustainability. Define and own large programs spanning multiple engineering and product teams across organizations - driving cross-functional alignment on AgentCore's most critical initiatives.

Operate in deep ambiguity where the business and architectural strategy may not yet be defined; drive clarity and create the path forward.

Our team values curious builders who are obsessed about customer experience, think long-term, and are excited to define the future of the Agentic platform.

We foster a collaborative, inclusive environment where diverse perspectives drive better solutions—and where the best ideas win regardless of where they originate. We ship fast and iterate with purpose

We believe work should be meaningful and fun—you'll be part of a team that takes pride in making history at the forefront of Agentic AI.

location: Warsaw, Indiana, United States of America
description:
At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at

As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. Job Function:

People Leader

All Job Posting Locations:

Alaska (Any City), California (Any City), Hawaii (Any City), Idaho (Any City), Nevada (Any City), Oregon (Any City), Remote (US), Warsaw, Indiana, United States of America, Washington (Any City)

Job Description:

We are searching for the best talent to join our DePuy Synthes team as a Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization to support the West Region (WA, ID, OR, CA, NV, HI, AK). This is a field-based role available in the United States. While specific cities are listed in the Locations section for reference, please note that they are examples only and do not limit your application.


Purpose:

DePuy Synthes is shaping the future of digital surgery. As the VELYS ecosystem continues to expand, our competitive advantage is our ability to turn every installation into a successful, growing robotic program that delivers lasting value for surgeons, health systems, and patients. That advantage is built in the field, one launch, one surgeon, and one clinical team at a time.

The Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization, is a hands-on player-coach responsible for clinical excellence, launch execution, and leading VELYS Clinical Specialists (VCSs) within an assigned region. The role drives account activation, not coverage: every launch should change how a surgeon operates and leave the account more capable than when it started.

Reporting to the Sr. Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization, this leader owns day-to-day clinical operations from pre-launch readiness through sustained adoption, connecting clinical execution with account strategy and turning field activity into insights that help the region operate proactively.


Key Responsibilities:

Lead Clinical Excellence & Launch Execution

  • Serve as the senior clinical expert in the region and model the standard for exceptional VELYS execution.
  • Maintain an active launch workload, personally leading assigned account launches and stepping in on strategic, complex, and escalated surgeon launches.
  • Engage early in pre-launch planning to understand the surgeon pipeline, implementation requirements, and expectations established during capital acquisition.
  • Translate regional priorities into clinical execution plans, ensuring the right VCS is deployed to the right account at the right time.
  • Run every LEEP Launch on a disciplined six-week rhythm, from installation and VELYS Core Activation Training through first cases and handoff to Field Sales.
  • Lead advanced troubleshooting, workflow optimization, and LOOP interventions for accounts requiring additional support.
  • Maintain expert-level proficiency across VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution (VRAS) TKA and UKA, VELYS Hip Navigation AI (VHN), and future digital applications, and uphold Instructions for Use (IFU), surgical technique, and clinical standards.

Lead & Develop VELYS Clinical Specialists

  • Directly manage and develop a regional team of VCSs, providing timely performance feedback, career development discussions, and individualized development plans.
  • Coach through field observations, launch participation, and procedural feedback, building the judgment and end-to-end ownership each launch requires.
  • Lead onboarding, simulation, and advanced clinical training to a consistent national standard, accelerating readiness for independent launch execution.
  • Own day-to-day clinical operations for the region, ensuring workflows, performance metrics, and compliance requirements are met within established timelines and budgets.
  • Lead Airtable CRM activity within your Area.
  • Identify and prepare high-potential VCSs for expanded responsibility, building the next generation of VELYS leaders.
  • Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, curiosity, continuous improvement, and customer focus.

Accelerate Surgeon Adoption & Utilization

  • Use procedural trends, log file reviews, and field observations to identify early adoption risk, explain why performance is changing, and determine the right clinical intervention.
  • Help surgeons progress from initial adoption toward confident, independent robotic proficiency.
  • Partner with the Sr. Manager and Utilization teams to execute plans for utilization recovery, surgeon conversion, and sustained adoption.
  • Maintain surgeon-level visibility into active users and non-users, surfacing barriers and conversion opportunities before they become escalations.
  • Identify growth opportunities through additional surgeons, VELYS applications, and technology upgrades, and bring them to the Sr. Manager and commercial partners early.

Strengthen ISO Clinical Capability

  • Equip qualified ISO partners to independently support appropriate workflows while maintaining DePuy Synthes clinical standards, serving as their trusted clinical resource.
  • Transition mature accounts toward appropriate local self-sufficiency, deploying clinical resources where expertise is needed and avoiding long-term dependency.

Partner with Customers & Across the Business

  • Build trusted relationships with surgeons, operating room teams, and hospital stakeholders, and provide the clinical perspective for executive business reviews and strategic account planning.
  • Resolve clinical escalations at the regional level wherever possible, engaging the Sr. Manager early on complex account challenges.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Education, Marketing, Field Service, Utilization, and Commercial Operations from pre-launch planning through sustained adoption, so customers experience one DePuy Synthes.
  • Provide a forward view of launch readiness, account health, VCS capacity, and capability gaps to inform launch prioritization and resource allocation.
  • Give leadership a clear read from the field: what is happening, why it matters, what is likely to happen next, and what action is recommended.
  • Solve what can be solved at the Manager and VCS level, and surface systemic barriers with evidence and a recommended path forward.
  • Communicate changes in customer support strategy, process, and technology to the team, ensuring VCSs understand what is changing and why.

Qualifications / Requirements:

What You’ll Bring

  • Demonstrated expertise supporting complex robotic-assisted orthopedic procedures, with expert-level knowledge across robotic and digital surgery workflows and the VELYS ecosystem.
  • Experience coaching and developing high-performing clinical professionals.
  • Ability to balance direct customer engagement with people leadership and regional execution.
  • Ability to influence surgeons, commercial partners, and hospital stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Proficient at managing relationships and expectations with our Independent Sales Organization (ISO) network.
  • Strong business acumen and understanding of capital technology adoption.
  • Proactive ownership of log file reviews and platform adoption, translating procedural data into clear priorities and actions for your team.
  • Proficiency with CRM, analytics, and automation, and curiosity about emerging technologies.
  • Clear, direct communication that balances empathy with high accountability.

Travel Requirements

  • Ability to travel up to 50% within the assigned region, driven by active LEEP Launch, LOOP, and VCS field responsibilities, and up to 60% overall in support of strategic launches, field coaching, surgeon education, utilization initiatives, and cross-regional clinical support.

How We Lead

  • Move with Heart: Bring safety, stability, and trusted guidance to your accounts. Lead with empathy and integrity, protect patients, and elevate surgeons.
  • Move as One: Stay calm when variables shift in the operating room. Communicate openly, seek out others’ expertise, and succeed and learn together as one DePuy Synthes.
  • Move to Win: Take full ownership of your outcomes. Eliminate ambiguity, prioritize resources intentionally, and navigate high-stakes environments with conviction.
  • Move the Future: Exercise patience for mastery, because true mastery takes repetition. Technology is the engine; hospitality, expertise, and trust are what win.

The Impact

The Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization, is more than a people leader. This role is the region's clinical multiplier, developing stronger VCSs, building more capable commercial partners, accelerating surgeon independence, and ensuring every strategic launch lays the foundation for sustained adoption and lasting value from the customer’s capital investment. By turning exceptional individual execution into a repeatable standard, this leader builds the capacity and insight that let the business shift from reactive to proactive.


Remote work options may be considered on a case-by-case basis and if approved by the Company.

About DePuy Synthes (DS)

Fueled by innovation at the intersection of biology and technology, we’re developing the next generation of smarter, less invasive, more personalized treatments.

Are you passionate about improving and expanding the possibilities of DS? Ready to join a team that’s reimagining how we heal? Our DS teams help keep more than 6 million people moving each year while delivering clinical and economic value to surgeons and healthcare systems. Our teams build solutions for joint reconstruction; trauma and craniomaxillofacial; sports, extremities, and elective foot and ankle; spine; and robotics and digital surgery.

Your unique talents will help patients on their journey to wellness. Learn more at

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopaedics business to establish a standalone orthopaedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. title: Master Data Management Operator
description:
Master Data Management Operator


The protector of data quality

Are you detail-oriented, structured and motivated by making data accurate, reliable and useful?

We are looking for a Master Data Management Operator to join our team and help ensure that critical master data is managed consistently across the organisation. In this role, you will be responsible for the daily creation, maintenance, enrichment, modification and archiving of master data in different business systems.

Master data is the foundation for efficient processes, reliable reporting and informed decision-making. Your work will help ensure that employees and systems can rely on accurate information about the organisation’s products, materials, suppliers, customers, assets, locations and other key business entities.


What you will do

  • Create, update, modify, enrich and archive master data in relevant systems.
  • Process master data requests according to approved procedures, policies and service levels.
  • Validate requests and supporting documentation before making changes.
  • Apply data standards, classifications, naming conventions and business rules.
  • Identify incomplete, inaccurate, duplicated, obsolete or inconsistent data.

title: Governance, Risk, and Compliance Specialist, AWS Security
description:
G'day! You've found an opportunity that could define your next chapter.

Applicants must be Australian citizens and hold or be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Security Clearance with the ability to successfully complete an Organisational Suitability Assessment. More information regarding security clearances can be found at https://www.agsva.gov.au/.

The Mission - Why This Program, Why Now?

You're joining at the defining moment of one of the most significant technology programmes Australia has ever undertaken. This programme will build and operate the dedicated cloud giving Australia's national security community and its allies the capability to see more, share more, innovate and act faster than ever before.

The architectural decisions being made now - how we structure networking, implement security controls, and automate at scale - will shape how Australia's national security community operates for the next decade. You won't be inheriting someone else's design choices. You'll be making them.

Your Opportunity
Imagine being the person who stands at the intersection of sovereign cloud innovation and the security frameworks that protect a nation. As a Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Specialist within AWS Security, you won't just be ticking boxes — you'll be the driving force behind the certification, accreditation, and authorisation activities that give Australia's national security community the confidence to operate at the speed of mission.

This role puts you in the room where it happens. You'll implement ISM, PSPF, DSPF, ASIO T4, and NIST frameworks into real-world cloud architectures — not as an afterthought, but as foundational design decisions. You'll collaborate with internal teams and customers to establish security baselines, define control objectives, and shape the security posture of a capability that will serve Australia for decades.

You'll bring your domain expertise to bear as a thought leader, developing material on cloud and emerging technologies that positions the organisation at the forefront of the industry. You'll exercise sound judgment in navigating the tension between short-term delivery and long-term security goals, demonstrating the resilience and composure needed to achieve great outcomes in complex environments.

The team you're joining is exceptional — security professionals drawn from both national security and private sector backgrounds, united by diversity of thought, creativity, and a relentless bias for action. Here, there are no "perfect" security solutions. There's continuous improvement, creative problem-solving, and the satisfaction of building something that genuinely matters.

Whether your career followed a traditional path or took a different route, what matters is what you bring today and where you want to go tomorrow. This is a place where curiosity is valued, mentorship is embedded in the culture, and your growth trajectory is limited only by your ambition.

Key job responsibilities
You'll be the GRC engine for designated physical and logical components within the cloud capability — owning assurance and authorisation activities end-to-end and ensuring every element adheres to the standards and protocols that underpin national trust.

Your work begins at the design table. You'll collaborate with internal teams and customers to establish security baselines, level-set requirements, and define the control objectives that shape how the capability is built. When ISM, PSPF, DSPF, ASIO T4, or NIST frameworks need to be woven into architecture, you'll be the one translating regulatory intent into engineering reality.

You'll create, optimise, and champion cross-functional working groups that drive security efficiency across the organisation. These aren't bureaucratic committees — they're high-performing teams solving real problems at pace, and you'll be the catalyst that keeps them focused and effective.

Your domain expertise won't stay locked in assessment reports. You'll develop thought leadership material on cloud and emerging technologies, contributing to the organisation's knowledge base and strengthening its position in the industry. Your insights will inform decisions well beyond your immediate team.

Deadlines will be tight and the stakes will be high. You'll deliver with exceptional attention to detail, ensuring accuracy across every aspect of security management while maintaining the momentum the programme demands.

You'll also serve as a mentor and advisor to teams across AWS, sharing your expertise and elevating the security capability of the broader organisation. Your influence will compound over time — building not just compliant systems, but a culture of security excellence.

A day in the life
Your morning kicks off with a cross-functional stand-up where you're briefing the team on an upcoming authorisation milestone. You've mapped the evidence requirements, identified the gaps, and you're assigning actions with the confidence of someone who's done this before — but the intellectual challenge of a capability that's genuinely new.

Mid-morning, you're deep in a working session with an engineering team, translating ASIO T4 and ISM controls into practical design decisions for a component build. They're grateful for your clarity — you have a gift for making complex frameworks feel navigable, and your input shapes their architecture in real time.

Before lunch, you're reviewing a draft security baseline document with a customer stakeholder. The conversation is collaborative, not adversarial — you've built the trust that comes from consistently delivering sound judgment and clear communication. Together, you're level-setting expectations and aligning on the path to authorisation.

The afternoon brings focused deep work: you're developing a thought leadership piece on an emerging cloud security challenge, drawing on your domain expertise to articulate a position that will inform the organisation's strategy. It's the kind of work that stretches your thinking and builds your professional reputation.

Late in the day, you're mentoring a colleague from another AWS team who's navigating their first accreditation cycle. You remember what it was like, and you're paying forward the guidance that accelerated your own growth. You log off knowing today mattered — to the programme, to your team, and to your career.

About the team
Why Amazon Security
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

The team is comprised of security professionals with a cross section of national security and private sector experience, providing a range of perspectives required for creative problem solving. We value diversity of thought, creativity, and a strong Bias for Action and Earn Trust. We believe that there are no "perfect" security solutions and we develop and iterate using a continuous improvement process.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Benefits
- Learning & development - AWS training and certification support, access to internal learning platforms.
- Health, income protection and life cover - Amazon subsidises private health insurance premiums, and group salary continuance and life insurance are included at no cost to you.
- Military differential pay launching in Australia - Australian employees taking defence reserve leave may receive up to 52 weeks of military differential pay to help cover the difference in pay while serving.
- Employee Assistance Program - Free, confidential support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for you and your family - mental health, financial coaching, legal questions, and everyday life events.
- Family-building benefit - Access to Maven for fertility treatment, adoption support, surrogacy, and parenting coaching.
- Amazon Extras & employee discount - cashback and discounts across hundreds of retail, fitness, travel, and lifestyle partners.

title: Software Engineer, Model Lifecycle and Signals
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, MODEL LIFECYCLE AND SIGNALS

As a Software Engineer on the Model Lifecycle and Signals team at SpaceXSI, you'll own the bridge between frontier models and every user-facing Cursor product, used at a scale few teams ever see. You'll decide when we use which model, spot where models go off track and build the guardrails to keep them on it, and shape what the next generation of models should learn. This role sits at the intersection of infrastructure, data, and product: you'll bring models from preview to production, dig into real-world data to find out what's actually working, and partner with research, inference, product, and data science teams to turn that evidence into better products and better models. Every improvement you make compounds across our products and every model we ship.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Get new frontier models into users' hands the day they're ready, and retire old ones without anyone noticing

  • Evaluate internal and external preview models before launch and give meaningful feedback to the teams building them

  • Build Cursor Router (https://cursor.com/docs/cursor-router): decide which model handles each request, balancing quality, speed, and cost at massive scale

  • Build the eyes and ears of the product, and the experimentation platform that puts them to work: signals that show where each model shines, where it goes off track, and what "better" actually means

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Track record of shipping production systems people rely on, owning problems end to end, and automating painful processes rather than repeating them

  • Experience building and operating evaluation, measurement, or model serving systems, such as AI evals, experimentation, ranking/relevance, or routers

  • Ability to turn ambiguous "quality" questions into concrete metrics, pipelines, and decisions

  • Fluency with data and the ability to collaborate effectively with data scientists and researchers

  • Taste and real curiosity about model and agent behavior, including trying new models the day they come out and forming opinions about where each one shine

$140,000 - $225,000 USD

title: Lead Technical Program Manager, Critical Facility Operations
description:
Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services.

This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation.

Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference.

The Role

Reporting to the Director of Critical Facility Operations, this role establishes and leads the technical programs that enable Cerebras’ capacity to enter service safely, operate reliably and scale consistently. Combining practical data center engineering and operations experience with strong program leadership and lessor engagement expertise, the role translates operational requirements into executable programs, clear commitments and measurable outcomes, across internal teams, colocation providers and service partners.

Responsibilities

  • Lead CFOps operational readiness for incoming sites, coordinating staffing and service coverage, maintenance arrangements, spares, training, operating procedures, monitoring, escalation paths and turnover documentation.

  • Engagement with colocation providers, understanding operational needs and translating contractual obligations into working responsibilities, service reviews, escalation mechanisms and action plans, in partnership with internal stakeholders responsible for capacity delivery and Cerebras services.

  • Develop and operationalize needed operational programs, including definitions, command, communications, response exercises, reviews, RCAs, and project execution.

  • Establish the CFOps program portfolio, priorities, ownership, milestones, dependencies, and reporting.

  • Coordinate operational acceptance with engineering, construction, commissioning and receiving operations teams, ensuring gaps and residual risks are documented and presented to the appropriate decision owners.

  • Engage with leadership and executives on state of Operations and be able to effectively communicate with clarity and drive actional next steps for our team and across the company (across business teams and functions).

  • Work in partnership with Operational engineering on program development and maturity, providing programmatic and execution support.

  • Represent CFOps during site evaluation, contract development, expansions and renewals, partnering with Acquisition, Contracts and Engineering to define operational requirements, assess gaps in provider commitments, and establish mitigations before commitments are made.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in mission-critical infrastructure, including data center operations, engineering, construction, or technical program management.

  • Proven experience leading complex programs across multiple sites, global teams, and cross-functional organizations.

  • Strong technical background in electrical, mechanical, or controls systems, gained through direct operational or engineering responsibility in data centers.

  • Experience working with lessors or colocation providers.

  • Demonstrated success building, implementing, and sustaining programs adopted by operational teams.

  • Working knowledge of data center white space, including servers, storage, networking equipment, racks, and associated data hall infrastructure.

  • Strong incident management, operational readiness, and executive communication skills.

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering or equivalent practical experience.

How the role will grow

As the portfolio expands, this role will likely evolve into leadership of the CFOps technical program-management function and business operations, building a team and extending standardized programs across regions. Its scope will grow to include availability and reliability program management and integrating reliability planning, maintenance and asset-management improvement, provider performance, operational tooling and portfolio-wide risk reduction. This role will involve heavy travel to sites in the first year of the role. Travel expectations, especially long-term are negotiable.

Team environment and culture

Cerebras is scaling at a tremendous pace and requires a team player who can handle a balance between driving maturity for the future and handling near-term ambiguity with a bias toward getting things done for the good of the team, with the goal of building and maturing the program over time into a resilient, effective and efficient operations organization. The ideal candidate will strike a balance between contributing, making sound decisions when needed, and providing data, information and clarity for others to make sound decisions, and be able to navigate between the three.

Location:

Fully remote, with up to 50% travel in the first year required.

Why Join Cerebras

People who are serious about software make their own hardware. At Cerebras, we have built a breakthrough architecture that is unlocking new opportunities for the AI industry. With dozens of model releases and rapid growth, we’ve reached an inflection point in our business. Members of our team tell us there are five main reasons they joined Cerebras:

  1. Build a breakthrough AI platform beyond the constraints of the GPU.

  2. Publish and open source their cutting-edge AI research.

  3. Work on one of the fastest AI supercomputers in the world.

  4. Enjoy job stability with startup vitality.

  5. Our simple, non-corporate work culture that respects individual beliefs.

Find out more about what it's like to work at Cerebras here!

Apply today and become part of the forefront of groundbreaking advancements in AI!

title: Crane Operator
description:
Somos una compañía global, líder en el desarrollo de infraestructuras regenerativas que generan un impacto positivo en la sociedad. Nuestra plantilla, formada por más de 65.000 profesionales y presente en más de 40 países de los cinco continentes, contribuye a nuestra misión de diseñar un planeta mejor. Buscamos personas que quieran marcar la diferencia, promover el desarrollo sostenible y encontrar soluciones a los mayores desafíos globales, incluidos el cambio climático, la sobrepoblación y la escasez hídrica. Únete a nosotros en la búsqueda de soluciones para lograr un futuro sostenible.

ACCIONA is looking to hire two Crane Operators for the TenneT projects within its Industry business area, under the ACCIONA Netherlands division.

Descripción del puesto

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Crane Operator is a skilled worker responsible for the safe operation of mobile cranes and ancillary lifting equipment used on high-voltage substation and transmission line projects.

The role requires a strong commitment to safety, the ability to work in complex industrial environments, and ongoing coordination with supervisors, lifting supervisors, technicians, foremen and other project personnel.

In addition to crane operations, the role holder will assist with general construction, installation and logistics activities as required by the project.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Typical duties and responsibilities include:

  • Operate mobile cranes safely and efficiently to lift, position and install equipment, steel structures, transformers, gas-insulated switchgear (GIS), cable drums and other project materials.
  • Carry out daily inspections and pre-use checks of the crane and its ancillary equipment.
  • Check the condition of lifting accessories, slings, shackles, spreader beams and other lifting gear.
  • Carry out lifting operations in accordance with approved lifting plans and established work procedures.
  • Check ground conditions and access routes, ensure the crane is stable, and verify that support pads and outriggers are correctly positioned.
  • Coordinate with lifting supervisors, signallers, riggers, technicians and site management.
  • Complete operating, inspection and maintenance records for assigned equipment.
  • Report incidents, unsafe conditions, equipment defects and any deviations identified.
  • Actively participate in safety meetings, daily briefings and risk assessments.
  • Keep assigned equipment clean and in good working order.
  • Ensure compliance with company and client health, safety and environmental requirements.

SUPPORT FOR SITE OPERATIONS AND TECHNICAL TEAMS

When no lifting operations are scheduled, the Crane Operator will assist construction, installation and commissioning teams with tasks appropriate to their training and experience, including:

  • Assist high-voltage technicians with electromechanical installation work.
  • Assist with the installation of primary and secondary substation equipment.
  • Handle and distribute materials on site.
  • Assist with cable laying and cable management.
  • Assist with the erection of steel structures and supports.
  • Assist with logistics and material storage activities.
  • Help prepare and set up work areas.
  • Carry out auxiliary tasks in support of start-up and commissioning teams.
  • Carry out general construction and site maintenance activities.
  • Participate in site housekeeping activities.

Requisitos del candidato

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Candidates must meet the following requirements:

  • Proven experience as a mobile crane operator on industrial, energy or construction projects.
  • A valid crane operator licence or certificate that meets the requirements of applicable regulations.
  • Knowledge of load charts, operating diagrams and lifting procedures.
  • Knowledge of the safety requirements applicable to lifting operations.
  • Ability to work on electrical infrastructure and high-voltage substation projects.
  • A sufficient command of English to understand work instructions and technical documentation and to pass TCVT certification in English

REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION

All candidates must submit:

  • An up-to-date CV.
  • Copies of all current crane operator licences and certificates.
  • Copies of training certificates relating to lifting operations.
  • Applicable health and safety training certificates.
  • Professional references, when requested.

Applications will not be considered unless the relevant supporting documentation is provided.


DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The following will be particularly valued:

  • Previous experience in high-voltage substations (110 kV, 150 kV, 220 kV, 380 kV or above).
  • Experience on electricity transmission, renewable energy or energy infrastructure projects.
  • Previous experience operating the following equipment:
    • Mobile elevating work platforms (Manlift / MEWP).
    • Telescopic handlers (Telehandler).
    • Forklift trucks (Forklift).
  • Training as a rigger, banksman or signaller.
  • VCA, SCC or equivalent certifications.
  • Basic knowledge of electromechanical installation.
  • Basic Dutch language skills.
  • Experience working for transmission system operators (TSOs) and electricity companies such as TenneT, Elia, National Grid, Amprion, 50Hertz or similar organisations.

Note: Manlift, Telehandler and Forklift certificates are not mandatory, but previous experience using this equipment in high-voltage substations will be considered a significant advantage. Where necessary, the company may provide the training required to obtain these certificates.


KNOWLEDGE

  • Lifting operations and load handling.
  • Interpreting lifting plans and studies.
  • Lifting accessories and rigging techniques.
  • Safety regulations applicable to crane operations.
  • Safety requirements in high-voltage substations.
  • Inspection and basic maintenance of mobile equipment.
  • Site logistics and materials management.

SKILLS

  • Safe and efficient operation of mobile cranes.
  • Interpreting load charts and lifting plans.
  • Working in complex industrial environments.
  • Effective communication with supervisors, technicians and site teams.
  • Identifying risks and implementing preventive measures.
  • Ability to work as part of multidisciplinary teams.
  • Flexibility to carry out support duties when no lifting operations are scheduled.
  • Organising and maintaining inspection documentation and operating records.

Job Description:

We are searching for the best talent to join our DePuy Synthes team as a Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization to support the Southeast Region (FL, GA, SC, NC, TN, AL, MS). This is a field-based role available in the United States. While specific cities are listed in the Locations section for reference, please note that they are examples only and do not limit your application.


Purpose:

DePuy Synthes is shaping the future of digital surgery. As the VELYS ecosystem continues to expand, our competitive advantage is our ability to turn every installation into a successful, growing robotic program that delivers lasting value for surgeons, health systems, and patients. That advantage is built in the field, one launch, one surgeon, and one clinical team at a time.

The Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization, is a hands-on player-coach responsible for clinical excellence, launch execution, and leading VELYS Clinical Specialists (VCSs) within an assigned region. The role drives account activation, not coverage: every launch should change how a surgeon operates and leave the account more capable than when it started.

Reporting to the Sr. Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization, this leader owns day-to-day clinical operations from pre-launch readiness through sustained adoption, connecting clinical execution with account strategy and turning field activity into insights that help the region operate proactively.


Key Responsibilities:

Lead Clinical Excellence & Launch Execution

  • Serve as the senior clinical expert in the region and model the standard for exceptional VELYS execution.
  • Maintain an active launch workload, personally leading assigned account launches and stepping in on strategic, complex, and escalated surgeon launches.
  • Engage early in pre-launch planning to understand the surgeon pipeline, implementation requirements, and expectations established during capital acquisition.
  • Translate regional priorities into clinical execution plans, ensuring the right VCS is deployed to the right account at the right time.
  • Run every LEEP Launch on a disciplined six-week rhythm, from installation and VELYS Core Activation Training through first cases and handoff to Field Sales.
  • Lead advanced troubleshooting, workflow optimization, and LOOP interventions for accounts requiring additional support.
  • Maintain expert-level proficiency across VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution (VRAS) TKA and UKA, VELYS Hip Navigation AI (VHN), and future digital applications, and uphold Instructions for Use (IFU), surgical technique, and clinical standards.

Lead & Develop VELYS Clinical Specialists

  • Directly manage and develop a regional team of VCSs, providing timely performance feedback, career development discussions, and individualized development plans.
  • Coach through field observations, launch participation, and procedural feedback, building the judgment and end-to-end ownership each launch requires.
  • Lead onboarding, simulation, and advanced clinical training to a consistent national standard, accelerating readiness for independent launch execution.
  • Own day-to-day clinical operations for the region, ensuring workflows, performance metrics, and compliance requirements are met within established timelines and budgets.
  • Lead Airtable CRM activity within your Area.
  • Identify and prepare high-potential VCSs for expanded responsibility, building the next generation of VELYS leaders.
  • Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, curiosity, continuous improvement, and customer focus.

Accelerate Surgeon Adoption & Utilization

  • Use procedural trends, log file reviews, and field observations to identify early adoption risk, explain why performance is changing, and determine the right clinical intervention.
  • Help surgeons progress from initial adoption toward confident, independent robotic proficiency.
  • Partner with the Sr. Manager and Utilization teams to execute plans for utilization recovery, surgeon conversion, and sustained adoption.
  • Maintain surgeon-level visibility into active users and non-users, surfacing barriers and conversion opportunities before they become escalations.
  • Identify growth opportunities through additional surgeons, VELYS applications, and technology upgrades, and bring them to the Sr. Manager and commercial partners early.

Strengthen ISO Clinical Capability

  • Equip qualified ISO partners to independently support appropriate workflows while maintaining DePuy Synthes clinical standards, serving as their trusted clinical resource.
  • Transition mature accounts toward appropriate local self-sufficiency, deploying clinical resources where expertise is needed and avoiding long-term dependency.

Partner with Customers & Across the Business

  • Build trusted relationships with surgeons, operating room teams, and hospital stakeholders, and provide the clinical perspective for executive business reviews and strategic account planning.
  • Resolve clinical escalations at the regional level wherever possible, engaging the Sr. Manager early on complex account challenges.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Education, Marketing, Field Service, Utilization, and Commercial Operations from pre-launch planning through sustained adoption, so customers experience one DePuy Synthes.
  • Provide a forward view of launch readiness, account health, VCS capacity, and capability gaps to inform launch prioritization and resource allocation.
  • Give leadership a clear read from the field: what is happening, why it matters, what is likely to happen next, and what action is recommended.
  • Solve what can be solved at the Manager and VCS level, and surface systemic barriers with evidence and a recommended path forward.
  • Communicate changes in customer support strategy, process, and technology to the team, ensuring VCSs understand what is changing and why.

Qualifications / Requirements:

What You’ll Bring

  • Demonstrated expertise supporting complex robotic-assisted orthopedic procedures, with expert-level knowledge across robotic and digital surgery workflows and the VELYS ecosystem.
  • Experience coaching and developing high-performing clinical professionals.
  • Ability to balance direct customer engagement with people leadership and regional execution.
  • Ability to influence surgeons, commercial partners, and hospital stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Proficient at managing relationships and expectations with our Independent Sales Organization (ISO) network.
  • Strong business acumen and understanding of capital technology adoption.
  • Proactive ownership of log file reviews and platform adoption, translating procedural data into clear priorities and actions for your team.
  • Proficiency with CRM, analytics, and automation, and curiosity about emerging technologies.
  • Clear, direct communication that balances empathy with high accountability.

Travel Requirements

  • Ability to travel up to 50% within the assigned region, driven by active LEEP Launch, LOOP, and VCS field responsibilities, and up to 60% overall in support of strategic launches, field coaching, surgeon education, utilization initiatives, and cross-regional clinical support.

How We Lead

  • Move with Heart: Bring safety, stability, and trusted guidance to your accounts. Lead with empathy and integrity, protect patients, and elevate surgeons.
  • Move as One: Stay calm when variables shift in the operating room. Communicate openly, seek out others’ expertise, and succeed and learn together as one DePuy Synthes.
  • Move to Win: Take full ownership of your outcomes. Eliminate ambiguity, prioritize resources intentionally, and navigate high-stakes environments with conviction.
  • Move the Future: Exercise patience for mastery, because true mastery takes repetition. Technology is the engine; hospitality, expertise, and trust are what win.

The Impact

The Manager, VELYS Clinical Utilization, is more than a people leader. This role is the region's clinical multiplier, developing stronger VCSs, building more capable commercial partners, accelerating surgeon independence, and ensuring every strategic launch lays the foundation for sustained adoption and lasting value from the customer’s capital investment. By turning exceptional individual execution into a repeatable standard, this leader builds the capacity and insight that let the business shift from reactive to proactive.


Remote work options may be considered on a case-by-case basis and if approved by the Company.

Fueled by innovation at the intersection of biology and technology, we’re developing the next generation of smarter, less invasive, more personalized treatments.

Are you passionate about improving and expanding the possibilities of DS? Ready to join a team that’s reimagining how we heal? Our DS teams help keep more than 6 million people moving each year while delivering clinical and economic value to surgeons and healthcare systems. Our teams build solutions for joint reconstruction; trauma and craniomaxillofacial; sports, extremities, and elective foot and ankle; spine; and robotics and digital surgery.

title: Regulatory Escalations, Amazon Flex, Service Level Standards
description:
Amazon Flex works directly with independent contractors – called delivery partners – to make deliveries to our customers. With Amazon Flex, individuals can now be their own boss delivering Amazon packages. Amazon Flex is powered by a mobile app that works in concert with our advanced logistics systems that allows delivery partners to on-board, schedule delivery times, guide them through their deliveries with in-app mapping and navigation, and more.

Amazon Flex's Service Level Standards (SLS) team is seeking a Senior Program Manager to own regulatory escalations within our Critical Operations function. This role exists to ensure every regulatory response is accurate, complete, and delivered within mandated timelines — while building the scalable processes needed.

As a Regulatory Escalations Program Manager, you will be the single-threaded owner for Amazon Flex's response to regulatory inquiries and investigations related to delivery partner enforcement. You'll manage the end-to-end lifecycle of each inquiry — from intake and scoping, through evidence gathering and record production, to final coordinated response with legal, compliance, and public policy teams. A single inquiry can require production of entire record categories across defined timelines, spanning weeks of sustained effort and coordination across multiple teams. This role requires someone who can manage complex, multi-week deliverables under strict deadlines while maintaining the precision and coordination that regulatory responses demand.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end lifecycle of all regulatory inquiries and investigations related to delivery partner enforcement — from intake and scoping through record production, review, and final response.
- Track and report on regulatory inquiry volumes, response times, inquiry types, and trends for Amazon's most senior leadership.
- Manage regulatory response timelines and SLAs, ensuring every deliverable is accurate, complete, and submitted within mandated windows.
- Coordinate with legal, public policy, and compliance teams.
- Build and maintain standardized processes, templates, and playbooks for regulatory response — transforming what is currently ad hoc into a repeatable, scalable function.
- Provide closed-loop feedback to enforcement program owners on patterns and themes emerging from regulatory inquiries — ensuring findings inform program design and reduce future exposure.
- Prioritize effectively across concurrent inquiries with competing deadlines.

  • Strong clinical or scientific background in neuroscience, rare disease, mood disorders
